Systems goals concern the organization’s survival, stability and effective functioning.

Thus, the answer is societal, output and systems.

qs.stem: A major distinction between line and staff units concerns

opts.A: the amount of resources each is allowed to utilize
opts.B: linkage of their jobs to the goals of the firm
opts.C: their linkage to the outside world
opts.D: none of these

qs.sol:
Line units directly carry out activities linked to the firm’s primary goals; staff units advise and support line units.

Thus, the major distinction concerns the linkage of their jobs to the goals of the firm, rather than resource allocation or contact with the outside world.

qs.stem: Control involves all but

opts.D: selecting Human Resource

qs.sol:
Control involves establishing goals or standards, measuring actual results against them, and taking corrective action when needed.

Selecting Human Resource belongs to staffing, not controlling. Therefore, it is the activity excluded here.

qs.stem: The division of labour through the formation of work units or groups within an organisation is called

opts.D: coordination

qs.sol:
Horizontal specialization divides an organisation’s work into distinct tasks and groups. Vertical specialization divides authority across hierarchical levels.

Here, labour is divided by forming work units or groups, so the answer is horizontal specialization.

qs.stem: The set of mechanisms used to keep actions and outputs within predetermined limits is called

opts.D: formalization

qs.sol:
Control is the set of mechanisms used to keep actions and outputs within predetermined limits.

The question describes keeping activities and results within set boundaries, so the answer is control.

qs.stem: Which among the following is an essential step in organising process ?

opts.D: Job evaluation

qs.sol:
Organising involves assigning duties and granting the authority needed to perform them.

Delegation of authority gives employees the power to carry out their assigned responsibilities. Hence, delegation of authority is an essential step in the organising process.

qs.stem: The causes of resistance to change, based on the emotions, tendencies and expectations of the people are called -

opts.D: Social causes

qs.sol:
Psychological causes of resistance to change arise from people’s emotions, tendencies and expectations.

The question specifically names these internal factors, so the answer is Psychological causes.

qs.stem: The system approach includes -

opts.D: Process, Input, Output and Criteria

qs.sol:
The systems approach views a system as a cycle of input, process, output and feedback.

Input provides resources or information; the process transforms them into output. Feedback evaluates the output and guides improvements.

Hence, the answer is Input, Process, Output and Feedback.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a component of “SWOT Analysis”?

opts.D: Options

qs.sol:
SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats.

Threats, Strengths and Weakness are components of SWOT. The O stands for Opportunities, not Options. Therefore, Options is not a component.

qs.stem: How can resistance to change be reduced?

opts.D: Effective leadership

qs.sol:
Resistance to change decreases when people understand the change, trust their leaders and feel supported.

Effective leadership provides clear communication, addresses concerns and encourages participation. Increased workload, overcontrol and fear of financial loss can instead increase resistance.

Therefore, the answer is Effective leadership.

qs.stem: The first step of control process is -

opts.D: Determining the reason for deviation

qs.sol:
The control process begins by setting goals and standards that serve as benchmarks for measuring performance.

Actual performance is then appraised, deviations are analysed, and corrective action is taken. Therefore, the first step is Establishment of goals and standards.

qs.stem: “Management is the development of people, not the direction of things.” This statement was given by -

opts.D: F. W. Taylor

qs.sol:
Management as the development of people emphasizes nurturing employees’ abilities rather than merely directing tasks and resources.

Lawrence A. Appley expressed this people-centred view in the statement, “Management is the development of people, not the direction of things.” Hence, the answer is Lawrence A. Appley.

qs.stem: Who among the following is the author of the book 'Work and Motivation'?

opts.D: Chris Argyris

qs.sol:
'Work and Motivation' (1964) is Victor H. Vroom's book, in which he set out expectancy theory: Motivation = Valence × Instrumentality × Expectancy.

The other thinkers' best-known books are Motivation and Personality (Maslow), The Human Side of Enterprise (McGregor) and Personality and Organization (Argyris).

topics.deep:
- **Nature of management:** goal-oriented, universal, multi-dimensional (work, people, operations), continuous process, both **art and science**, a profession of sorts. Importance: achieves group goals, increases efficiency (reduces costs, raises productivity), creates dynamic organisation, develops society.
- **Levels:** Top (strategic planning, policy), Middle (departmental heads, tactical), Lower/operational (supervisors, foremen).
- **Functions and sequence:** Planning -> Organising -> Staffing -> Directing -> Controlling (planning is first and controlling the last function; co-ordination is the essence that binds all functions). Directing includes supervision, motivation, leadership, communication.
- **Schools of thought:**
| Thinker | Contribution |
|---|---|
| F.W. Taylor | Scientific management: time, motion and fatigue study; standardisation; differential piece rate; functional foremanship; mental revolution |
| Henri Fayol | Administrative management; 5 functions (POCCC) and **14 principles** |
| Max Weber | Ideal bureaucracy: hierarchy, rules, impersonality, merit-based selection |
| Elton Mayo | Human relations (Hawthorne studies) |
| Gulick & Urwick | POSDCORB |
| Peter Drucker | MBO |
| Herbert Simon | Decision making |
- **Fayol's 14 principles:** division of work, authority & responsibility, discipline, unity of command, unity of direction, subordination of individual interest, remuneration, centralisation, **scalar chain**, order, equity, stability of tenure, initiative, esprit de corps. **Gang plank** = direct cross-link between same-level employees without breaking the scalar chain.
- **Motivation theories:**
| Theory | Key idea |
|---|---|
| Maslow | Hierarchy: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation; lower need satisfied first |
| Herzberg | Hygiene factors (salary, conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (recognition, achievement, work itself, advancement) create satisfaction |
| McGregor | Theory X (people dislike work) vs Theory Y (self-directed) |
| Alderfer | ERG: existence, relatedness, growth |
| Vroom | Expectancy: valence x expectancy x instrumentality |
- **Leadership:** autocratic (all decisions by leader), democratic/participative, laissez-faire (free-rein). **Managerial Grid** (Blake & Mouton): 1,1 impoverished; 9,1 task; 1,9 country club; 5,5 middle; **9,9 team management**.
- **Organisation:** Line, line-and-staff (staff gives expert advice to line managers), functional, matrix. **Span of control** depends on nature of work, ability, nature of tasks; **delegation** = authority + responsibility; accountability cannot be delegated. **Unity of command** = one employee takes orders from one boss.
- **Decision making:** Simon - intelligence, design, choice. Techniques: brainstorming, Delphi. Planning steps: objectives -> premises -> alternatives -> evaluation -> selection -> derivative plans -> implementation -> follow-up.
- **Control process:** standards -> measure -> compare -> find deviation -> corrective action; tools: budgets, MIS, break-even.
- **Contemporary:** TQM (customer focus, continuous improvement), Kaizen, JIT, lean (elimination of seven wastes), outsourcing, quality circles, Six Sigma.
- **HRM:** recruitment (attracting), selection (choosing), training (current job skills) vs development (future roles), appraisal; staffing; job description (tasks) vs job specification (qualifications).
- **Ethics & CSR:** Sec 135 applies to companies with net worth >= Rs 500 crore, or turnover >= Rs 1000 crore, or net profit >= Rs 5 crore; spend at least 2% of average net profit of previous three years; committee of three or more directors.

**Likely question angles:** (1) Which are managerial functions (coding/testing are not). (2) Full form of POCCC / POSDCORB letters. (3) Match thinker with idea. (4) Identify principle (gang plank, esprit de corps, scalar chain). (5) Herzberg motivators vs hygiene. (6) Maslow's order. (7) Managerial Grid styles. (8) Step in control or planning process. (9) Features of delegation. (10) Difference between line and staff.

topics.title: 3. Business Foundations, Organisation Forms & Entrepreneurship
topics.theory:
- **Commerce** = trade + aids to trade (banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising); **mining is an extractive industry**, not a component of commerce. Business > Commerce > Trade.
- **Sole proprietorship:** simplest form; unlimited liability, full control, quick decisions. **HUF:** headed by **Karta**.
- **Partnership (Act 1932):** agreement-based, mutual agency (each partner is **agent and principal**), unlimited liability; **nominal partner** lends name only; **sleeping partner** gives capital but takes no active part.
- **Company (Act 2013):** private = 2 to 200 members; **public = minimum 7 members**; **OPC** = one member + nominee. **MoA** = constitution/objects; **AoA** = internal rules.
- **Government company** = govt holds at least **51%** paid-up capital. Oldest form of public enterprise = **departmental undertaking**; also statutory corporation.
- **Co-operative society:** minimum 10 members, one-member-one-vote, registered.
- **Entrepreneur:** innovator (**Schumpeter**); types: innovative, imitative, Fabian, drone; **intrapreneur** = entrepreneur within an organisation.
- **MSMED Act 2006** (in force Oct 2006) classifies micro, small, medium enterprises by investment and turnover.
- **Marketing mix (4 Ps):** product, price, place, promotion; sales promotion boosts short-term sales. Franchising = right to use brand for a fee.
- **Business environment:** PESTLE; macro factors (economic, social, political, legal, technological) vs micro; globalisation, tax jurisdiction = legal-political factors.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a component of commerce?

opts.D: Warehousing

qs.sol: Commerce covers trade and aids to trade such as insurance, transport, and warehousing. Mining is an extractive industry that produces goods, rather than facilitating trade.
qs.rel: Commerce = trade + aids to trade (transport, banking, insurance, warehousing); mining is an extractive industry. Neighbours: primary, secondary, tertiary industry.

qs.stem: In a public limited company, the minimum number of shareholders is ______.

opts.D: Ten

qs.sol: CONCEPT: Company law fixes different minimum membership thresholds for different company types at the time of formation. (In ordinary public-company usage, "shareholder" and "member" refer to the same person — every shareholder of record is a member.) Under Section 3(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, a private company must be formed with at least two members, while a public company must be formed with at least seven members; there is no upper limit on membership for a public company. …
qs.rel: A public company needs at least 7 members; private 2 (max 200). Neighbours: minimum directors (3 vs 2), OPC with one member.

qs.stem: Which document defines the scope and objectives of a company and serves as its constitution?

opts.D: Memorandum of Association

qs.sol:
A company’s constitutional documents separate its founding particulars and permitted objects from the rules governing its internal management.

Under the Companies Act, 2013, the memorandum states the objects for which a company is incorporated; the articles contain regulations for its management.

Application

The question asks for the document defining the company’s scope and objectives. Those are its objects, stated in the Memorandum of Association. The memorandum is therefore the constitutional charter meant here.

Contrast

Articles of Association sets out the company’s internal management regulations. …
qs.rel: Memorandum of Association defines objects and scope and is the company's charter; Articles hold internal rules. Neighbours: prospectus, certificate of incorporation.

qs.stem: Which document is mandatory for incorporation of a One Person Company (OPC)?

opts.D: Partnership Deed

qs.sol: Incorporation requires constitutional documents including articles of association. The other documents belong to different business forms or later stages.
qs.rel: Incorporation of an OPC needs constitutional documents including articles of association with a nominee. Neighbours: MoA, minimum one director.

qs.stem: Who is considered the father of entrepreneurship?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

In entrepreneurship theory, an entrepreneur is not merely a business owner; the defining economic role is to introduce innovation and reorganize resources in a new way.

Schumpeter explained this process through new combinations and creative destruction: innovations replace older products, methods, or markets and thereby drive economic development.

Application

Joseph Schumpeter gave the foundational theoretical account that links the entrepreneur with innovation and economic change. This is why standard entrepreneurship literature associates the title in the question with Joseph Schumpeter. …

qs.stem: The minimum number of members required to form a public company is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Under section 3(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, a public company is formed by seven or more persons.

The statutory minimum concerns initial subscribers; the maximum number of members is a different question.

qs.stem: The application for registration of a small-scale unit should be submitted to the

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A District Industries Centre handles local registration and support for small-scale industrial units.

Its General Manager is the district-level receiving authority for the application in this examination context.

qs.stem: The MSME Development Act came into force in

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was enacted in 2006.

That is the year identified for the Act’s coming into force among the choices.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the context for entrepreneurship?

opts.A: Entrepreneurship takes place in small businesses.
opts.B: Entrepreneurship takes place in large businesses.
opts.C: Entrepreneurship takes place in a wide variety of contexts.
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Entrepreneurship means recognising and organising an opportunity, which can occur in small firms, large firms and other settings.

The broad statement includes those settings; the narrower statements describe only particular cases.

qs.stem: PSEs are organizations owned by

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
PSE means public sector enterprise.

A public authority or government has the controlling ownership in such an enterprise.

Private family and foreign-company ownership do not make an enterprise public-sector.

qs.stem: Retailers who have no fixed place of sale are called

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Itinerant retailers move from place to place rather than selling from a fixed shop.

Street and market traders describe narrower forms or locations; the general class requested is itinerant retailers.

qs.stem: ‘‘I really believe that entrepreneurship is about being able to face failure and succeed after failure.’’ Who said this?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The quoted view treats failure as something an entrepreneur learns from before succeeding. In the paper’s attribution, this statement is by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, the founder of Biocon.

qs.stem: A person who works within an organization and having entrepreneurial capabilities is called

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
An intrapreneur works inside an established organization while applying initiative and innovation associated with entrepreneurship.

The organizational setting distinguishes this role from an independent founder.

qs.stem: The MSMED Act which addresses the issues relating to medium scale and service related enterprises’ definition, credit, marketing and technology upgradation came into force on

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was enacted in 2006 but brought into force on 2 October 2006.

The question asks for commencement, so the relevant month and year are October 2006, not the date of enactment or an earlier year.

qs.stem: _______ entrepreneurs are extremely task-oriented.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Technical entrepreneurs concentrate on developing and applying a product or process with specialist know-how.

Their attention to executing technical work makes them strongly task-oriented.

qs.stem: The process of grouping users into market segments based on the desirable consequences sought from the product is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Benefit based segmentation groups buyers by the outcome they seek from a product.

The stem specifies the benefit sought, so the narrower marketing term applies.

qs.stem: The actual or prospective purchaser of products or services is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A customer is the person who actually buys, or may buy, a product or service.

A consumer may use the product, and a user may operate it, without being its purchaser.

qs.stem: What measures has the government taken to solve the problem of finance and marketing in the small-scale sector?

opts.A: Setting up of Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
opts.B: Providing credit guarantee scheme for MSMEs
opts.C: Launching of Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
SIDBI is a dedicated institution for finance and development of small industries.

The credit guarantee scheme eases collateral-related access to loans.

PMEGP supports new microenterprises with credit-linked subsidy; several listed measures therefore apply.

qs.stem: A name, term, design, symbol, or any other feature that identifies one seller’s good or service as distinct from those of other sellers is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A brand is an identifying name, symbol, design, or similar feature.

Its purpose is to distinguish one seller’s offering from competitors’ offerings.

Both parts of the definition point to a brand.

qs.stem: An organized network of agencies and institutions which, in combination, perform all the functions required to link producers with end customers to accomplish the marketing task is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A distribution channel is the network of intermediaries connecting producers to end users.

Its members perform selling, logistics, and related marketing functions.

That full network matches the definition in the stem.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an example of a financial barrier to entrepreneurship?

opts.B: Limited access to capital and funding
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The official BPSC final answer key for TRE 1.0, 2023, PGT Entrepreneurship, Series A, Question 64 selects “Lack of market demand”. In standard textbook usage, “limited access to capital and funding” is the typical example of a financial barrier. This question follows the commission’s final answer key.

qs.stem: A favourable set of circumstances that creates a need for a new product, service or business is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
An opportunity is a favourable set of circumstances that creates room for a new offering or venture.

A niche is a particular market segment, while a venture is the business undertaken after recognizing the opening.

qs.stem: Powers, rights, remuneration, qualification and duties of directors are discussed clearly in which of the following documents?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The memorandum states a company’s constitution and external objects. The articles govern its internal management, including directors’ powers, duties, qualifications and remuneration. A prospectus instead invites investment from the public.

qs.stem: If the wife and husband are running a business venture together, they are called as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A married couple jointly operating one venture are termed copreneurs, combining couple and entrepreneurs. The relationship and joint operation are both essential.

qs.stem: A consumer good and/or service (such as soap, candy bar and shoeshine) that is bought frequently, often on impulse, with little time effort spent on the buying process, is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Convenience products are purchased often and with minimal comparison or effort.

Soap and small impulse purchases fit that pattern.

The frequency and low effort identify the convenience class.

qs.stem: Which of the following is recognized as a misconception about entrepreneurship?

opts.B: Entrepreneurship is found only in small businesses
opts.C: Successful entrepreneurship needs only a great idea
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the printed word “not” makes every listed claim a misconception while the final key selects the collective response; “not” was removed in both languages.

Entrepreneurship requires sustained work, occurs in firms of many sizes, and needs more than an idea.

Thus all three stated claims are misconceptions, so the collective response applies.

qs.stem: A person who starts an industrial unit by means of an innovative skill is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The BPSC Series A final answer key records “first generation entrepreneur” for the printed question.

qs.stem: The mix of controllable variables that a firm uses to reach desired sales level in target market is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The marketing mix combines controllable marketing decisions used to reach a target market.

It includes product, price, place, and promotion.

The stem describes that complete mix rather than one component.

qs.stem: In assessing the financial resources needed for a proposed venture, what is the first step?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:

qs.stem: Which of the following promotional tools is thought to be the most expensive to use?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Promotional cost can be compared per customer contact.

Personal selling needs a salesperson’s time for each interaction, unlike mass messages.

That labour makes it generally the costliest tool per contact.

qs.stem: Permission for distribution of services in another country under a specific copyright and tight control over operations is called

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Franchising permits a party abroad to distribute services using the franchisor's brand and business format while the franchisor controls operating standards.

Ordinary licensing grants use of intellectual property but generally does not impose that full operational format and close control.

qs.stem: A proposed name of company for registration is considered undesirable, if

opts.B: it resembles closely with the name of an existing company
opts.C: it is an emblem of the Government of India, United Nations, etc.
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.stem: Which of the following could provide an individual with the motivation to start with a new business venture?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Financial return can reward the risk and work of a new venture.

Independence can motivate someone to control their own decisions.

A willingness to take risk can also drive venture creation, so several stated motives apply.

qs.stem: Which of the following features is characterized an economic activity?

opts.C: Sale or exchange of goods and services
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Economic activities are undertaken to earn a livelihood or income.

Producing goods or services and selling or exchanging them are business activities; work for salary or wages is employment.

Each is an economic activity, so the combined response covers the listed cases.

qs.stem: The primary objective of sales promotion is to

opts.C: generate immediate sales and boost revenue
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Sales promotion uses short-term inducements to prompt a near-term purchase.

Its primary immediate aim is a sales lift, whereas durable brand equity and loyalty are longer-term outcomes.

qs.stem: Which of the following are common myths about entrepreneurs?

opts.C: Everyone has the potential to be an entrepreneur
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the final key marks the multiple-statements answer, while the printed “not a common myth” makes only the statement about everyone’s potential fit; the negation was removed.

Treating entrepreneurs as gamblers and claiming they are born rather than made are both common myths. Entrepreneurial abilities can be developed, so the universal-potential statement is not one of those myths.

qs.stem: Huge industrial organizations extending their industrial and marketing operations through a network of own branches in many countries are known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.stem: A person who undertakes those ventures which go well along with the changing demand in the market is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A modern entrepreneur adapts the venture to changing market demand and customer needs. The description emphasizes responsiveness to current demand, not family background or merely production.

qs.stem: Which of the following protocols was followed related to banning the use of chlorofluorocarbon, bromine and chlorine compounds?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The Montreal Protocol controls ozone-depleting substances, including chlorofluorocarbons and halons containing bromine.

Its phase-out commitments target damage to the stratospheric ozone layer, which distinguishes it from climate-emission agreements.

qs.stem: In which business, the support service activities are categorized?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

Support services such as transport, banking and insurance belong to the tertiary or service sector.

Primary activities extract resources; secondary activities manufacture goods; the service-sector category is absent from the named choices.

qs.stem: The specific act of acquiring organizational sanction and committed resources to achieve innovative results within an existing firm is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: its broad “entrepreneurial activities” wording also allowed the umbrella term for internal entrepreneurship; the stem now asks for the specific act named in the final key.

Intrapreneuring denotes carrying an internally sponsored innovation through organizational approval and resource commitment.

qs.stem: A group of people leading the way in new developments or ideas is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A vanguard is the leading group at the forefront of a movement or new development.

The description emphasizes leading the way, not merely showing enthusiasm or following a group.

qs.stem: _____ is conducted to determine whether a proposed business has sufficient management expertise, organizational competence and resources to successfully launch its business.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Organizational feasibility tests whether the proposed venture has the people, management skills, structure and resources to launch. Financial feasibility tests funding and returns; market feasibility tests demand and competition.

qs.stem: The personnel in chain stores have to obey the instructions received from

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Chain stores use centralised control over their branches.

Branch staff follow policies and operating instructions issued by the head office.

qs.stem: Which retail business acts as a universal supplier of a wide variety of products?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A departmental store brings many departments and product lines under one roof.

That broad assortment makes it a general or universal supplier to shoppers.

qs.stem: Which product-specific marketing term names arranging for a product to occupy a clear, distinctive and desirable place relative to competing products in the minds of the target market?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the final key names market positioning, but the printed definition describes product positioning; the stem now asks for the most specific product-level term and the key is corrected.

The object being placed in customers’ minds is a product, relative to competing products.

The specific marketing term for that task is product positioning.

qs.stem: Cooperative societies are compulsorily registered under which of the following Acts?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The Cooperative Societies Act of 1912 supplied the general legal framework for registering cooperative societies in British India. The 1922 year is not the cited enactment, and contract law governs agreements rather than cooperative registration. State cooperative laws also operate today, but the historical Act asked about is the 1912 statute.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of a sole proprietorship?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A sole proprietor can start with few formalities and keeps the residual profit, giving a direct incentive.

Independent ownership also gives a sense of personal accomplishment. Several listed advantages therefore apply.

qs.stem: Which one of the following is not a challenge for the entrepreneur?

opts.A: Managing the cash flow of their business
opts.C: Choosing the product or service to sell in the market
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E
Concept

An entrepreneurial challenge is a decision, constraint, or operating problem that must be managed while starting and running a venture.

Typical challenge areas include liquidity, staffing, and market-offering fit; classify each activity by the business function it affects.

Application

Apply that classification to the listed activities:

Managing cash flow concerns the timing of receipts and payments and the venture's ability to meet obligations; it is a financial-management challenge.

Recruiting employees concerns finding and selecting suitable people; it is a human-resource challenge. …

qs.stem: A business plan is important for

opts.A: providing lenders and investors assurance that they will earn a descent returns
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: its final key marks no listed use, although the printed choices include a genuine use; the key is corrected to the business-presentation function.

A plan can present a venture to funders and partners. It cannot guarantee returns, and it is not an instrument for purchasing goods.

qs.stem: _____ type of entrepreneurs is particularly important for the underdeveloped countries because they contribute significantly to the development of such nations.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Adoptive, or imitative, entrepreneurs transfer and adapt innovations already developed elsewhere. That diffusion helps less-developed economies build industry without having to invent every technology locally.

qs.stem: The purpose of soft loan scheme is to encourage units to undertake

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A soft loan offers concessional finance to improve productive assets.

Plant and machinery may be modernized, replaced when obsolete, or renovated to restore efficiency. Several listed uses therefore fit the scheme.

qs.stem: The Registrar of Companies allots a CIN to the company after completion of all legal formalities for its registration. What is the full form of CIN?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The Registrar assigns a unique identifier to a registered company.

CIN expands to Corporate Identity Number: it identifies the corporate entity; it is distinct from the certificate issued on incorporation.

qs.stem: What are the 6 C’s that motivate entrepreneurs to establish their own business?

opts.A: Change, challenge, creativity, control, curiosity and cash
opts.B: Customer, challenge, creation, control, curiosity and cash
opts.C: Connect, conversation, contact, consideration, consumption and community
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The entrepreneurship mnemonic lists change, challenge, creativity, control, curiosity and cash as six motives for starting a venture. Each is a personal or economic attraction of independent enterprise.

qs.stem: The form of organization which a public enterprise may take is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A public enterprise may operate as a departmental undertaking directly within government or as a statutory corporation created by legislation.

A cooperative society is owned and controlled by its members. Thus several listed organizational forms fit a public enterprise.

qs.stem: ——— are network of retail shops that are owned and operated by manufacturers dealing in standardized and branded consumer products.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A chain-store system operates several similar retail outlets under common ownership and control.

Manufacturers can use these outlets to sell standardised, branded products with consistent policies and prices.

qs.stem: Which of the following contracts is signed by the promoters during the promotion of the company with the third party on behalf of the proposed company?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Before incorporation, the company has no legal existence and cannot itself contract.

Promoters therefore enter a preliminary, or pre-incorporation, contract with a third party for the proposed company.

qs.stem: Which of the following is true about statutory corporations?

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A statutory corporation is created by a specific legislative act and has its own legal identity and powers.

Its accounting and audit arrangements follow its statute rather than ordinary departmental rules, and its staff are generally employees of the corporation.

Consumer cooperative societies are formed to protect consumers from exploitation by traders and middlemen. They ensure that consumers get goods of standard quality at reasonable prices and promote fair trade practices.

qs.stem: What is the full form of CWC?

More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.stem: Under section 13(4) of the Companies Act, 2013, which change of a company’s registered office necessarily requires prior approval of the Central Government?

None of the above

Section 13(4) requires Central Government approval for moving a registered office from one State to another. A change stated only in terms of cities need not cross a State boundary.

qs.stem: Products that are unknown to the potential customers or they are known product which customers do not actively seek are known as

qs.stem: Which one of the following is the Not-for-Profit Organization?

qs.stem: A prospectus filed with the Registrar of Companies to invite public subscription is issued by

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:

A prospectus invites the public to subscribe to a company’s securities. Only a public company seeking such investment makes that invitation. A public company that raises no public subscription need not issue one.

qs.stem: Which of the following is the best example of relationship marketing by a firm?

opts.A: Developing a long-term relationship with individual customers for mutual benefit
opts.B: Using public relations tools to communicate with the target audience
opts.C: Focusing on the use of print media to build broad reach
opts.D: Focusing on short-term gains through one-time transactions

qs.sol:
Relationship marketing is a strategic orientation in which a firm builds and sustains an ongoing relationship with individual customers over the long term, aiming for continued engagement and mutual benefit to both the business and the customer - rather than optimising for a single sale or the widest possible audience reach.

Applying this to the options: developing a long-term relationship with individual customers for mutual benefit is exactly this orientation put into practice, so it is the best example of relationship marketing among those offered. …

qs.stem: The process which involves gauging a customer’s requirements and designing a product or service to serve that requirement is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Marketing starts by identifying customers’ needs and designing an offering that meets them.

The stem includes both understanding demand and shaping a product or service in response.

That combined process is marketing.

qs.stem: What is the purpose of using contests and sweepstakes in sales promotion?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Contests and sweepstakes invite participation around a brand and draw attention to it.

The promotion can therefore broaden brand awareness; collecting feedback or giving a price discount is a different mechanism.

qs.stem: Tax jurisdiction is an example of which environmental factor?

qs.stem: A business plan is important for all of the following reasons, except

It can project returns, but cannot assure lenders or investors that a return will actually be earned; that guarantee is the exception.

Marketing starts by identifying needs and wants, then creates an offering to satisfy them.

qs.stem: Which type of risk is involved if a product affects the mental health of the consumer?

qs.stem: Who are the primary risk bearers of the company ?

qs.stem: Environment Protection Act was enacted in the year

qs.stem: Statutory meeting must be conducted by the :

topics.deep:
- **Business, trade, commerce, industry:** Industry (primary extractive, genetic, secondary manufacturing/construction); **Commerce = trade + aids to trade** (transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising). Business is wider than commerce, which is wider than trade.
- **Features of economic activity:** undertaken to earn livelihood, involves money, legal; non-economic (love, patriotism) is not.
- **Forms of organisation:**
| Form | Minimum / Maximum | Liability | Key point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sole proprietorship | 1 | Unlimited | Easiest to form, quick decisions, limited capital |
| Partnership | 2 / 50 | Unlimited, joint and several | Mutual agency; Act 1932 |
| HUF | Family | Karta unlimited, others limited to share | Hindu Succession Act coparcener daughters equal rights (2005 amendment) |
| Co-operative society | 10 members | Limited | One member one vote; service motive |
| Private company | 2 / 200 | Limited | No public issue, share transfer restricted |
| Public company | 7 / no limit | Limited | Can invite public; min 3 directors |
| OPC | 1 + nominee | Limited | MoA and AoA mandatory for incorporation |
- **Company documents:** **MoA** = charter defining objects and scope (name, registered office, objects, liability, capital, association clause); **AoA** = internal rules; Prospectus (invites public); Certificate of Incorporation carrying **CIN**; directors' powers and duties are in AoA and the Act. Pre-incorporation contracts are signed by promoters. Statutory meeting is held by public companies; interval between two AGMs not above 15 months.
- **Public sector:** Departmental undertaking (oldest, e.g. Railways), statutory corporation (own Act), government company (>= 51% govt holding), Navratna etc. Privatisation, disinvestment, outsourcing.
- **Entrepreneurship:** Process of identifying opportunity, mobilising resources. Types by Danhof: innovative, imitative, Fabian, drone. Schumpeter - innovation; McClelland - need for achievement; intrapreneur (Pinchot). Myths: need huge capital, born not made, only risk-takers. Barriers: financial, technical, lack of experience, regulatory.
- **MSME:** MSMED Act 2006 (in force 2 Oct 2006); classification now based on investment plus turnover (2020: micro up to Rs 1 crore/5 crore, small up to 10 crore/50 crore, medium up to 50 crore/250 crore; limits revised upward again in 2025). Support: soft loans, SIDBI, NSIC, DIC.
- **Business plan:** needed for obtaining funds, guiding operations; steps: idea, feasibility study (market, technical, financial, managerial), project report, registration.
- **Marketing basics:** 4 Ps; market segmentation (demographic, geographic, psychographic, behaviour/benefit), targeting, **positioning**; products: convenience, shopping, specialty, unsought; branding, trademark; promotion mix: advertising (costly), personal selling, sales promotion, PR. Retailing: department store, supermarket, chain stores, hawkers (no fixed place), mail-order.
- **Business environment:** PESTLE; Porter's five forces (entry, buyers, suppliers, substitutes, rivalry); macro vs micro environment; Environment Protection Act 1986.
- **Social responsibility:** towards owners, employees, consumers, community; sustainability (Brundtland 1987).

**Likely question angles:** (1) Minimum members for public/private company, OPC. (2) Which document is mandatory for OPC/incorporation. (3) Which is not a component of commerce. (4) Advantages/disadvantages of sole trader and partnership. (5) Types of partners (nominal, sleeping, active). (6) Meaning of government company. (7) Entrepreneur type matching. (8) MSMED Act features. (9) Marketing mix elements. (10) Business environment factors classification.

topics.title: 4. Accounting Fundamentals: Journal, Ledger, Trial Balance & BRS
topics.theory:
- **Accounting** = identifying, recording, classifying, summarising and interpreting financial transactions; objectives: maintain records, find profit/loss, show financial position, provide information to users.
- **Accounting equation:** Assets = Liabilities + Capital (Owner's equity).
- **Golden rules:** Personal - debit the receiver, credit the giver; **Real - debit what comes in, credit what goes out**; Nominal - debit expenses/losses, credit incomes/gains.
- **Modern rule:** increase in assets/expenses = debit; increase in liabilities/capital/income = **credit**; decrease in assets is credited.
- **Journal** = book of original (first) entry, chronological. **Ledger** = principal book, analytical/classified record ("book of final entry").
- **Concepts:** entity, money measurement, going concern, cost, dual aspect, accrual, matching, **conservatism** (anticipate no profit, provide for all losses), consistency, materiality.
- **Permanent (real/personal) accounts** are balanced and carried forward; **temporary (nominal) accounts** are closed to P&L.
- **Drawings** by owner (cash or goods) are debited to Drawings A/c, not expenses.
- **Trial balance** checks arithmetical accuracy only; errors of omission, commission, principle and compensating errors do not disturb it; difference goes to **Suspense A/c**.
- **BRS** reconciles Cash Book and Passbook (cheques issued but not presented, cheques deposited but not collected, bank charges, interest/dividend collected by bank).

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the objective(s) of accounting?
 I. Maintenance of records of business transactions
 II. Calculation of profit and loss

opts.D: Neither I nor II

qs.sol:
Concept: Accounting is the systematic process of recording, classifying, summarising, and interpreting the financial transactions of a business. Its two primary objectives are (a) maintaining a permanent, verifiable record of every transaction, and (b) ascertaining the profit or loss and overall financial position of the business for a period.

Application: Statement I describes the bookkeeping function — recording each transaction in journals and ledgers so a permanent record exists. Statement II describes the analytical function — using that recorded data to prepare the Trading and Profit and Loss Account and determine whether the business earned a profit or incurred a loss. …
qs.rel: Objectives of accounting: keep systematic records, ascertain profit/loss, show financial position and give information to users. Neighbours: accounting equation, accounting cycle.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are correct?

 I. The Journal is the book for chronological record

 II. The ledger is the book for analytical record

opts.D: Neither I nor II

qs.sol: A journal records transactions chronologically, while a ledger classifies and summarizes them analytically under accounts. Both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Journal = original/chronological record; ledger = classified, analytical record (book of final entry). Neighbours: subsidiary books, posting, trial balance.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are correct? 

I. All permanent accounts are balanced and carried forward to the next accounting period. 

II. The temporary accounts are closed at the end of the accounting period.

opts.D: Neither I nor II

qs.sol:
Permanent accounts are balance-sheet accounts such as assets, liabilities, and capital. They are not closed at the end of the accounting period; their balances are carried forward to the next period.

Temporary accounts, such as revenue, expense, gain, and loss accounts, are closed at the end of the accounting period so that the next period starts with zero balances in those accounts.

Therefore, both statements I and II are correct.
qs.rel: Permanent (real/personal) accounts are balanced and carried forward; temporary (nominal) accounts close to P&L at year end. Neighbours: closing entries.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are the objectives of financial accounting?
 i) Proper recording of transactions
 ii) Ascertainment of the financial position
 iii) Reporting financial information
 iv) Defalcation prevention
 v) Digital marketing

opts.A: i, ii, iii and iv only
opts.D: i and ii only

qs.sol: Financial accounting records transactions, helps ascertain financial position, reports financial information, and supports control against defalcation. Digital marketing is not an objective of financial accounting.
qs.rel: Financial accounting: record transactions, ascertain financial position, report information to users. Neighbours: management accounting, cost accounting.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is correct?
 I. Decrease in asset is credited
 II. Increase in liabilities is credited

opts.D: Neither I nor II

qs.sol: In accounting, a decrease in assets is credited and an increase in liabilities is also credited. Therefore both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Decrease in assets is credited; increase in liabilities is credited. Neighbours: modern Dr/Cr rules, capital and income also credited on increase.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the reason(s) for difference between Cash Book and Bank Passbook?
 I. Cheques paid into the bank but not yet collected
 II. Interest and dividends collected by the bank

opts.D: Neither I nor II

qs.sol: Bank reconciliation exists because a business's Cash Book and the bank's Passbook do not update for every transaction at the same moment. Differences between the two fall into two recognized categories: (1) timing differences — amounts the business has already recorded but the bank has not yet processed (e.g., cheques deposited but awaiting clearance, or cheques issued but not yet presented), and (2) bank-originated entries — amounts the bank records first because only the bank has visibility into them (e.g., interest credited, dividends collected on the customer's behalf, bank charges, or standing-instruction debits), which reach the Cash Book only once the customer sees the statement. …
qs.rel: Differences between cash book and passbook: cheques deposited not collected, cheques issued not presented, bank charges, direct credits. Neighbours: BRS.

qs.stem: In case of a Real Account, the general rule of accounting is:

opts.A: Debit what comes in and credit what goes out
opts.B: Debit the giver and credit the receiver
opts.C: Debit the receiver and credit the giver
opts.D: Debit expenses or losses, credit incomes or gains

qs.sol: A real account records assets. Under the traditional rule, an asset entering the business is debited and an asset leaving is credited.
qs.rel: Real account rule: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Neighbours: personal and nominal account rules.

qs.stem: How should the withdrawal of goods from stock by the owner of the business, for personal use, be recorded in books of accounts of an entity?

opts.A: Debiting Drawing account and crediting cash account
opts.B: Debiting Purchases account and crediting capital account
opts.C: Debiting Capital account and crediting drawing account
opts.D: Debiting Drawing account and crediting purchases/stock account

qs.sol: Goods taken for personal use reduce business stock and count as owner drawings. Debit Drawings and credit Purchases or Stock for their cost.
qs.rel: Owner's withdrawal of goods is drawings: debit Drawings, credit Purchases. Neighbours: capital reduction, drawings are not an expense.

qs.stem: Economic life of an enterprise is split into the periodic interval as per

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:

Revenue, expenses and financial position can then be measured and reported for each period, even though the enterprise continues beyond it.

Application: The question asks which concept splits economic life into periodic intervals. That act of division is the periodicity concept, so periodicity is the answer.

Contrast: The related concepts perform different accounting functions:

Matching associates expenses with the revenue of a defined period; it uses a reporting period rather than creating one. …

qs.stem: The preparation of Trial Balance is for

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

A trial balance tests whether total ledger debits equal total ledger credits.

This can reveal arithmetic and posting mistakes that upset equality, but not every error of commission or principle.

qs.stem: While preparing Bank Reconciliation Statement, balance as per Passbook will have to be _____ or balance as per Cashbook _____ by the amount of direct payment by customers into Trader’s A/c with the banker.

More than one of the above

E

qs.stem: Irrespective of the time taken to produce or sell, an inventory is always considered to be a:

qs.sol: Inventory is normally expected to be sold or consumed in the operating cycle. It is therefore classified as a current asset.

qs.stem: Revenue from service contracts is recognized by:

opts.A: With reference to the stage of completion
opts.C: Only when the contract is fully completed
opts.D: On the basis of time proportion

qs.sol:
Revenue from service contracts is recognized based on the stage of completion of the service at the reporting date.  (Percentage of Completion Method) . This reflects work performed and revenue earned up to that point, even if payment has not been fully received.
 Common ways to measure progress: cost-to-cost (costs incurred ÷ total estimated costs), efforts expended (hours or labour), or output measures such as surveys or milestones.

opts.D:

The suit concerns a contract to supply goods in the ordinary course of trading.

Defending that contract protects current operations and creates no enduring asset.

qs.stem: Business paid to Mr. Anuj a cheque of ₹80,000 as salary on 25th June, 2023. Mr. Anuj went to bank to deposit cheque in his account on 3rd July, 2023. What is the entry to be passed in the Balance Sheet on the date of Final A/c?

opts.A:
Bank A/c … Dr.

To Outstanding Salary A/c
opts.B:
Salary A/c … Dr.

To Outstanding Salary A/c
opts.C:
Salary A/c … Dr.

To Anuj’s A/c
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

The cheque was issued to settle salary; the accounting entry on issue is debit Salary Expense and credit Bank.

Later presentation by the employee changes bank clearance, not the firm’s expense recognition.

A balance sheet does not require any of the displayed journal entries solely because the cheque is deposited later.

qs.stem: Furniture for a cloth dealer is a/an

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

qs.sol:
A cloth dealer buys furniture for use in the shop, not for resale as cloth inventory.

Furniture provides service over several accounting periods and is therefore a fixed asset.

qs.stem: The basic function of financial accounting is to

opts.D:
More than one of the above

None of the above

qs.sol:
Financial accounting first records transactions in books of original entry.

It then classifies them in ledger accounts and summarises them in statements.

Recording, classification and summarisation are all basic functions, so several named statements are true.

qs.stem: Revenue from sale of goods ordinarily is reported as a part of the earning in the period

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Under accrual accounting, sale revenue is recognised when the sale occurs and the earning process is complete.

Later collection settles a receivable; purchasing inventory is an earlier, separate transaction.

qs.stem: The statement containing various ledger balances on a particular date is known as

opts.D:

qs.sol:
Ledger accounts have debit or credit balances at a given date.

A trial balance lists those balances together to test arithmetical equality before statements are prepared.

qs.stem: The note which is sent to a customer when he returns the goods is known as

opts.D:

E

qs.sol:
When a customer returns goods to the seller, the seller reduces the customer’s receivable.

The seller communicates that credit through a credit note.

A debit note is normally issued by the buyer to notify the seller of goods returned.

qs.stem: Passbook is the statement of account of the customer maintained by the

qs.sol: A passbook records deposits, withdrawals and the resulting balance in the customer’s account. The bank keeps this account in its own books and issues the passbook or statement to the customer. The customer may reconcile it with personal records.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statements are true?

1. Prepaid rent is a Personal A/c.

2. Interest on Drawings is an income for the business.

3. Accrued income and income due but not received are same.

4. Cost of obtaining licence to carry out business is a capital expenditure.

Code:

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Prepaid rent is a representative personal account; interest on drawings is income to the business.

Accrued income means income earned but not yet received, and an enduring business licence is normally a capital cost.

Thus both listed three-statement combinations contain true statements.

qs.stem: A Bank Reconciliation Statement is a

opts.D:

E

None of the above

qs.sol:

Option E

Modified from the official paper: the final key marks “More than one of the above”, although none of the three named books contains a bank reconciliation statement; the key is corrected.

A bank reconciliation statement is prepared separately to explain differences between the cashbook bank balance and the passbook balance.

It is not a constituent of either book or the bank account.

qs.stem: According to the conceptual framework, the objectives of financial reporting are based on

opts.B: reporting on management’s stewardship and performance

Modified from the original question: the supplied key selected several listed bases, but the conceptual framework grounds general-purpose reporting in users’ information needs; the key is corrected to the residual choice. Conservatism is a cautious measurement concept, stewardship is an aspect of information sought, and accounting principles are standards rather than the objective’s foundation.

qs.stem: Accounting equation means

opts.C: Current Assets + Current Liabilities = Long-term Liabilities
opts.D:

E

qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: “Assets = Equities” omitted the liability claim and made the equality ambiguous; expanded that option to the full accounting equation. Assets are financed by creditors’ claims plus the owner’s residual claim.

qs.stem: Repairing incurred before using a second hand motor car purchased recently is a

opts.D:

E

qs.sol: Repairs necessary to put a recently bought used car into usable condition are part of its acquisition cost. They provide benefit over the vehicle’s useful life and are capitalized; ordinary later maintenance would be a period expense.
“पूर्ण होने की अवस्था का हवाला देते हुए” सेवा अनुबंध में काम की पूर्णता की अवस्था के अनुसार अर्जित राजस्व पहचाना जाता है। “भुगतान प्राप्त होने पर” भुगतान की तारीख अर्जन की अवस्था से अलग हो सकती है।

qs.stem: The debit side of a company’s trial balance totals ₹ 2000 more than the credit side. Which one of the following errors would fully account for the difference?

opts.A: A discount received of ₹ 1000 has been debited to discount allowed account.
opts.B: A receipt of ₹ 4000 for commission receivable has been omitted from the records.
opts.C: ₹ 1000 was paid for the plant maintenance has been correctly entered in the cash book and credited to the plant asset account.
opts.D: A receipt of ₹ 2000 for commission receivable has been omitted from the records.

qs.sol: “A discount received of ₹ 1000 has been debited to discount allowed account.” replaces a ₹ 1000 credit with a ₹ 1000 debit, producing the stated ₹ 2000 excess debit. “A receipt of ₹ 4000 for commission receivable has been omitted from the records.” omits equal debit and credit entries, so it cannot cause that difference. The same is true of “A receipt of ₹ 2000 for commission receivable has been omitted from the records.”

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा लेखांकन का कार्य नहीं है?

opts.A: व्यापारिक लेनदेन का रिकॉर्ड बनाए रखना
opts.C: निर्णय लेने के लिए जानकारी प्रदान करना
opts.D:
उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं

लेखांकन के प्रमुख कार्यों में लेनदेन का रिकॉर्ड रखना, लाभ या हानि की गणना करना और निर्णय लेने के लिए आवश्यक जानकारी देना शामिल है। इस प्रश्न में दिए गए पहले तीनों कार्य लेखांकन से संबंधित हैं। इसलिए उत्तर है: “उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं।”

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन लेखांकन सूचना की गुणात्मक विशेषता नहीं है?

opts.D:
उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं

qs.sol:

Option E

Relevance, reliability, and comparability are qualitative characteristics of accounting information. All three listed individual choices are such characteristics; therefore, none of them is a non-qualitative characteristic.

qs.stem: लेखांकन सिद्धांत जो बताता है कि समान मदों के लिए समान लेखांकन व्यवहार दिया जाना चाहिए, उसे कहा जाता है:

qs.stem: लेखांकन में ‘मिलान अवधारणा’ का पालन करने से निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा लाभ नहीं है?

opts.A: यह किसी अवधि के लिए वास्तविक लाभ या हानि का निर्धारण करने में मदद करता है
opts.B: यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि संबंधित खर्च उनके संबंधित राजस्व से मेल खाते हैं
opts.C: यह विभिन्न लेखांकन अवधियों में प्रदर्शन की बेहतर तुलना की अनुमति देता है
opts.D:
उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक

E

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

मिलान अवधारणा के अनुसार किसी अवधि के राजस्व से संबंधित खर्च उसी अवधि में दर्ज किए जाते हैं। इससे वास्तविक लाभ या हानि का निर्धारण और विभिन्न अवधियों के प्रदर्शन की तुलना बेहतर होती है। इसलिए दिए गए सभी पहले तीन कथन लाभ हैं; ऐसा कोई कथन नहीं है जो लाभ न हो—“उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं।”

qs.stem: खराब सामान के लिए ग्राहक को दिए गए भत्ते को रिकॉर्ड करने के लिए किस स्रोत दस्तावेज़ का उपयोग किया जाता है?

opts.D:

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं

आवेदन: यहाँ खराब सामान के कारण ग्राहक को भत्ता दिया गया है, इसलिए इसे जमा पत्र में रिकॉर्ड किया जाएगा।

qs.stem: इन लेनदेन में से किस लेनदेन का स्टॉकधारकों की समता पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ेगा?

opts.D:

शुद्ध घाटा समता को घटाता है।

qs.stem: व्यवसाय में मालिक द्वारा निवेश की गई राशि को जमा किया जाना चाहिए :

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी मद खाता बही के क्रेडिट पक्ष पर दिखाई देगी?

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी अशुद्धि तलपट में अंतर का कारण नहीं बनेगी?

opts.D:
उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक

E

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं

qs.stem: यदि तलपट के दोनों पक्ष मेल नहीं खाते हैं, तो कौन सा खाता खोला जाता है?

qs.stem: बैंक समाधन विवरण है:

opts.B: ग्राहक द्वारा तैयार किया गया विवरण
opts.C: बैंक द्वारा तैयार किया गया विवरण

उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं
