qs.stem: Which of the following Accounting Standards (AS) is related to cash flow statements?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

Accounting Standard AS–3 deals with cash flow statements.

The listed standards—AS–2 (Inventories), AS–4 (Contingencies and Events Occurring After the Balance Sheet Date), and AS–6 (Depreciation Accounting)—do not deal with cash flow statements.

Therefore, the answer is None of the above.

Cash inflow means cash received; cash outflow means cash paid.

Decrease in debtors generally means customers have paid their dues, bringing cash in.

Issue of shares brings in cash from investors.

Decrease in creditors generally means dues to suppliers have been paid, taking cash out.

Therefore, Decrease in creditors is not a cash inflow.

Correct Answer:
Option E

A cash outflow is money paid out; a cash inflow is money received.

Sales of goods bring in cash when payment is received.

Issue of debentures brings in cash from investors.

Dividend received brings in cash from investments.

None of these is a cash outflow, so the answer is None of the above.

Financial statements are based on facts recorded in the accounting books.

They summarise recorded transactions, rather than forecasts of future events. Hence, the answer is recorded facts.

Financial analysis evaluates a firm’s financial information to identify both its strengths and weaknesses.

It reveals strengths, such as sound profitability, and weaknesses, such as poor liquidity. Therefore, the answer is identifying the strengths and weaknesses of the firm.

Financial analysis uses techniques that reveal trends and assess a business’s financial position and performance.

Trend analysis tracks changes in financial figures over time.

A cash flow statement helps analyse cash inflows, outflows and liquidity.

Thus, both are used in financial analysis, so the answer is More than one of the above.

Ratio analysis uses relationships between financial figures to assess a business’s financial health and performance.

It helps analyse financial position, including liquidity and solvency.

It supports effective business control by identifying weaknesses and deviations from targets.

It enables comparative study of financial efficiency across periods or businesses.

All three objectives apply, so the answer is More than one of the above.

Solvency ratios assess a firm’s ability to meet its long-term financial obligations.

The debt-equity ratio compares debt with shareholders’ equity, showing how much the firm relies on borrowed funds. Therefore, it is a solvency ratio.

qs.stem: Break-even point is the point where

opts.A: fixed cost and variable cost lines intersect
opts.B: sales and total cost lines intersect
opts.C: variable and total cost lines intersect
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The break-even point is where sales revenue equals total cost, resulting in neither profit nor loss.

On a cost–revenue graph, this equality occurs where the sales and total cost lines intersect. Hence, the answer is sales and total cost lines intersect.
आन्तरिक निरीक्षण का उद्देश्य लेखा-कार्य को व्यवस्थित रखना और उसकी जाँच करना है। इसलिए इसमें लेखा तथा उसकी जाँच दोनों शामिल होती हैं।
आन्तरिक जाँच पद्धति संतोषजनक न होने पर लेन-देन की लगातार और विस्तृत जाँच आवश्यक होती है। इसलिए इस स्थिति में चालू अंकेक्षण उपयुक्त है।

नियम

CARO 2016 बैंकिंग कंपनियों, बीमा कंपनियों और एकल-व्यक्ति कंपनियों पर लागू नहीं होता।

अनुप्रयोग

दिए गए तीनों प्रकार की कंपनियाँ CARO 2016 के दायरे से बाहर हैं। इसलिए उत्तर है: **इनमें से कोई नहीं**।

कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 के प्रावधान कम्पनी के प्रकार के आधार पर सीमित नहीं हैं; ये निजी, सार्वजनिक और सरकारी कम्पनियों पर लागू होते हैं।

इसलिए दिए गए विकल्पों में उचित उत्तर है: सभी प्रकार की कम्पनी।

सिद्धांत: अंकेक्षक की स्वतंत्रता बनाए रखने के लिए वह अंकेक्षण और परामर्श जैसी सेवाएं दे सकता है, लेकिन स्वयं प्रबंधकीय कार्य नहीं कर सकता।

लागू करने पर, वैधानिक अंकेक्षण, चालू अंकेक्षण और परामर्श सेवा अंकेक्षक द्वारा दी जा सकती हैं। प्रबंध सेवाएं देना उसकी स्वतंत्रता और भूमिका के विरुद्ध है। अतः उत्तर: प्रबंध सेवाएं।

नियम

रेलवे कम्पनियों के अंकेक्षण में कंपनी के अन्तर्नियम, बहिर्नियम तथा रेलवे अधिनियम, 1990—सभी का संदर्भ लिया जाता है।

इसलिए उपयुक्त उत्तर है: सभी।

नियम: पूर्वदत्त व्यय चालू परिसंपत्ति है। इसमें कमी होने पर रोकड़ मुक्त होती है, इसलिए यह रोकड़ का स्त्रोत बनती है।

इसलिए उत्तर है: रोकड़ का स्त्रोत।
चिट्ठा अंकेक्षण का उद्देश्य बैलेंस शीट में दर्शाई गई सम्पत्तियों और दायित्वों की सत्यता तथा अस्तित्व की जाँच करना है। इसलिए इसमें सभी सम्पत्तियों एवं दायित्वों की जाँच होती है।

नियम: आन्तरिक अंकेक्षक औपचारिक प्रतिवेदन प्रस्तुत नहीं करता; वह स्वामी या प्रबन्धक को सुझाव देता है।

अतः “आन्तरिक अंकेक्षक का प्रतिवेदन” अमान्य है।
परीक्षण जाँच का सिद्धान्त है कि सभी लेखा-पुस्तकों की जाँच न करके चुनी हुई या खास-खास लेखा-पुस्तकों की जाँच की जाती है। इसलिए उत्तर है: खास-खास लेखा पुस्तकों की जाँच होती है।

लागत लेखांकन में उत्पादन या व्यवसाय संचालन से संबंधित लागतें शामिल की जाती हैं। सामान्य संचय को हस्तान्तरण विनियोजन है, दान लागत नहीं है और प्राप्त किराया आय है। इसलिए इनमें से कोई भी लागत लेखांकन में सम्मिलित नहीं की जाती।

संकल्पना: ऋण निधि में वे स्रोत शामिल होते हैं जिनसे संस्था ऋण प्राप्त करती है, जैसे डिबेंचर, ऋण और सार्वजनिक जमा।

इस सूची में कराधान के लिए प्रावधान ऋण प्राप्त करने का स्रोत नहीं है। इसलिए ऋण निधि में शामिल नहीं है: कराधान के लिए प्रावधान।

अवधारणा

प्रोप्राइटर फंड पर रिटर्न मालिक द्वारा लगाए गए धन के उपयोग और उससे प्राप्त लाभ को दर्शाता है।

अनुप्रयोग

यहाँ रिटर्न का संबंध मालिक निधि के उपयोग से है। इसलिए उत्तर है: मालिक निधि का उपयोग।

वित्तीय विवरणों का निर्वचन केवल विश्लेषण तक सीमित नहीं होता; इसमें उपलब्ध सूचनाओं की आलोचना, तुलना एवं प्रवृत्तियों का अध्ययन करके निष्कर्ष निकाला जाता है। इसलिए इसमें आलोचना एवं विश्लेषण, तुलना एवं प्रवृत्तीय अध्ययन तथा निष्कर्ष निकालना—तीनों शामिल हैं। अतः “उपयुक्त सभी” सही उत्तर है।

वित्तीय विवरण में संस्था की वित्तीय स्थिति और परिणाम से संबंधित प्रमुख विवरण शामिल होते हैं।

यहाँ आर्थिक चिट्ठा, लाभ-हानि खाता तथा संचालकों एवं अधिशेषकों का प्रति वेतन—तीनों दिए गए हैं। इसलिए उत्तर है: इनमें से सभी।

qs.stem: The verification of the authority and authenticity of transaction recorded in the books of accounts is called

opts.D: Investigation

qs.sol: Vouching is the audit procedure used to verify the authority, authenticity, and validity of transactions recorded in the books of accounts. Therefore, the answer is Vouching.

qs.stem: Auditing and Assurance Standard – 2 (AAS – 2) are concerned with

opts.D: Objective and scope of the audit of financial statements

qs.sol: AAS-2 establishes the objective and scope of an audit of financial statements. It explains the auditor’s responsibilities and the nature of the audit, so it concerns the objective and scope of the audit of financial statements.

qs.stem: Auditing begins where ______ ends.

opts.D: Year

qs.sol: Auditing verifies the accuracy and completeness of accounting records. Therefore, auditing begins where accounting ends: Accounting.

qs.stem: Name the audit, that is generally conducted between two annual audit.

opts.D: Final auditing

qs.sol: An interim audit is conducted during the accounting year, between two annual audits. Therefore, the audit generally conducted between two annual audits is interim auditing.

qs.stem: After completion of the audit of a company the auditor should submit its report to the

opts.D: Shareholders

qs.sol: An auditor’s report communicates the results of the audit to the company’s owners. After completing the audit, the auditor therefore submits the report to the shareholders.

qs.stem: A systematic examination of books and records of a business is called

opts.D: Checking

qs.sol: Auditing is the systematic examination of a business’s books and records. Since the question describes this complete examination, the answer is Auditing.

qs.stem: Fixed cost Rs. 12,00,000 (including depreciation Rs. 80,000); selling Price per unit Rs. 1,200; variable cost per unit Rs. 900; Loan Installment Rs. 2,00,000. Cash Break Even Point will be

opts.D: 4933 units

qs.sol:
Cash break-even point is calculated using cash fixed costs, so depreciation is excluded while the loan installment is included.

Cash fixed costs = Rs. 12,00,000 − Rs. 80,000 + Rs. 2,00,000 = Rs. 13,20,000.

Contribution per unit = Rs. 1,200 − Rs. 900 = Rs. 300.

Cash break-even point = Rs. 13,20,000 ÷ Rs. 300 = 4,400 units.

Thus, the answer is 4400 units.

qs.stem: An enquiry regarding the value, ownership, title, existence and possession of an asset is called

opts.D: Investigation

qs.sol: Verification is the audit process of establishing an asset’s existence, ownership, title, possession, and value. Since the enquiry covers all these aspects, it is called Verification.

qs.stem: Are increase in sales price

opts.D: Lowers net profit

qs.sol: Break-even point depends on fixed costs divided by contribution per unit. Increasing the sales price increases contribution per unit, while fixed costs remain unchanged. Therefore, fewer units are needed to cover fixed costs, so the break-even point is lowered: “Lowers Break-Even Point.”

qs.stem: An arrangement of staff duties whereby no one person is allowed to record every aspect of a transaction is called

opts.D: Internal Management

qs.sol: Internal check is a system of arranging duties so that no one employee handles every stage of recording a transaction. Therefore, the arrangement described is Internal Check.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a responsibility of the Audit Committee under the Companies Act, 2013?

opts.D: Recommend appointment of auditors

qs.sol:
Under Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Audit Committee’s responsibilities include examining financial statements, overseeing internal audit, and recommending the appointment of auditors.

Approval of share buyback schemes rests with the Board of Directors or shareholders, as applicable, under Section 68—not the Audit Committee.

Therefore, the answer is Approve share buyback schemes.

qs.stem: Break-Even Point is

opts.A: Where total revenue equals total costs
opts.B: Where total revenue equals total fixed cost
opts.C: Where total revenue equals total variable cost
opts.D: Where total revenue exceeds the total costs

qs.sol:
The break-even point is the level of sales at which a business makes neither a profit nor a loss.

Since profit is total revenue minus total costs, profit is zero when total revenue equals total costs.

Therefore, the answer is: Where total revenue equals total costs.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct ?

opts.A: Managerial accounting and cost accounting both are complementary to each other in nature
opts.B: Managerial accounting is concerned with the accounting information that is useful to management
opts.C: Managerial accounting includes details of quantitative information only
opts.D: Managerial accounting depends on cost accounting

qs.sol:
Managerial accounting uses both quantitative information, such as costs and profits, and qualitative information, such as employee morale and customer satisfaction, to help management make decisions.

Cost accounting supports managerial accounting, so the two are complementary. Managerial accounting also provides information useful to management.

Thus, the statement “Managerial accounting includes details of quantitative information only” is not correct because it excludes qualitative information.

Add administrative overheads to factory cost to obtain cost of production.

Therefore, the answer is Factory cost + Administrative overheads.

qs.stem: Sales budget is a

opts.D: none of these

qs.sol:
A functional budget relates to a specific business function, such as sales, production or purchasing.

A sales budget estimates sales for a given period, so it is a functional budget.

qs.stem: The difference between fixed and variable cost has a special significance in the preparation of

opts.D: none of these

qs.sol:
A flexible budget adjusts costs for different levels of activity, so it requires costs to be classified as fixed or variable.

Fixed costs remain unchanged within the relevant activity range, while total variable costs change with activity. This distinction allows a flexible budget to estimate total costs at each activity level.

Therefore, the answer is flexible budget.

qs.stem: Management Accounting deals with

opts.D: None of the (A) and (B)

qs.sol:

qs.stem: Which of the following institution is authorised for framing Standards for Auditing (SAs) in India?

opts.A: Institute of Cost Accountants of India
opts.B: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
opts.C: Institute of Company Secretaries of India
opts.D: Institute of Chartered Financial Analyst of India

qs.sol:
Standards on Auditing (SAs) lay down requirements for conducting audits.

In India, the Auditing and Assurance Standards Board of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) frames these standards. Hence, the answer is Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

qs.stem: “Cash Equivalents” includes -

opts.B: Preference shares matured after one year
opts.D: Money market deposits for very short period

qs.sol:
Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and carry insignificant risk of changes in value, normally with an original maturity of three months or less.

Money market deposits for a very short period meet these conditions. Cash-in-hand is cash itself, while preference shares maturing after one year and shares of unlisted companies do not qualify.

Hence, the answer is Money market deposits for very short period.

qs.stem: Management Accounting is mainly related with -

opts.D: Quantitative information only

qs.sol:
Management accounting provides information for planning, forecasting and managerial decision-making, so its main focus is the future.

Cost ascertainment mainly belongs to cost accounting. Management accounting uses past and present data to plan ahead and considers both quantitative and qualitative information.

Therefore, the answer is Projection for future.

Issuing bonus shares transfers reserves to share capital. Neither total shareholders’ equity nor debt changes.

|---|---|---|
| Current | CA/CL | 2:1, short-term solvency |
| Quick (acid test) | (CA - stock - prepaid)/CL | 1:1 |

| Net profit | NP/Net sales x 100 | Overall profitability |
| Debt-equity | Long-term debt/Equity (shareholders' funds) | Long-term solvency; commonly 2:1 maximum |
| Proprietary | Shareholders' funds/Total assets | Safety margin |
| Interest coverage | EBIT/Interest | Ability to pay interest |
| Stock turnover | COGS/Average stock | Slow turnover = weak demand |
| Debtors turnover | Net credit sales/Average debtors | Collection efficiency |
| ROCE | EBIT/Capital employed x 100 | Profitability |
| EPS | (PAT - preference dividend)/No. of equity shares | Per-share earning |
- **Worked example:** CA 3,00,000 (stock 1,00,000, prepaid 20,000), CL 1,50,000 -> current ratio 2:1; quick = (3,00,000 - 1,20,000)/1,50,000 = 1.2:1. Sales 10,00,000, GP 2,50,000 -> GP ratio 25%. GP 25% on cost = 20% on sales (25/125). Net profit 2,00,000, pref dividend 20,000, 90,000 shares -> EPS = 2.00.
- **Cash flow statement (AS-3 / Ind AS 7):** compulsory for listed/large companies.
| Activity | Examples |
|---|---|
| Operating | Cash from customers, salaries, income tax paid, adjustments of net profit |
| Investing | Purchase/sale of fixed assets, investments, interest/dividend received |
| Financing | Issue of shares/debentures, loans, repayment, dividend paid |
Indirect method: Net profit + depreciation + loss on sale - gain; decrease in current assets (stock, debtors, prepaid) adds, increase in current liabilities (creditors, bills payable) adds. Cash equivalents: short-term (maturity up to 3 months), highly liquid.
- **Cost accounting:** cost classification - material, labour, expenses; direct/indirect; fixed/variable/semi-variable. **Cost sheet:** Prime cost (DM + DL + direct expenses) + factory overhead = factory cost; + office overhead = cost of production; + selling and distribution = cost of sales. Example: Prime cost 20,000; factory overhead 25% of prime = 5,000 -> factory cost 25,000.
- **Marginal costing and CVP:** Contribution = Sales - Variable cost; P/V ratio = Contribution/Sales; **BEP (units) = Fixed cost/Contribution per unit**; BEP (value) = Fixed cost/P-V ratio; margin of safety = Actual sales - BEP sales. Example: SP 10, VC 6, FC 48,000 -> contribution 4 -> BEP = 12,000 units (Rs 1,20,000). Raising selling price lowers BEP; raising fixed cost raises BEP. Make-or-buy: buy only if the purchase price is below variable cost (when capacity is idle).
- **Standard costing:** Material price variance = (SP - AP) x actual qty; material usage = (SQ - AQ) x SP; **labour rate variance = (SR - AR) x actual hours**; efficiency variance = (SH - AH) x SR.
- **Management accounting:** internal use, future-oriented, non-statutory; includes both quantitative and qualitative information; distinction: financial accounting reports to outsiders per standards, cost accounting ascertains and controls cost.
- **Auditing:** systematic examination of books; begins where accounting ends. Types: statutory, internal, interim (between two annual audits), continuous, balance sheet audit. **Vouching** = verifying authority and authenticity of transactions; **verification** = existence, ownership, value of assets; **test checking** = selective sampling; internal check = system where no one person handles all steps of a transaction.
- **Company audit:** auditor appointed by shareholders at AGM (first auditor by Board), reports to members; term 5 years; SAs issued by ICAI (Auditing and Assurance Standards Board); CARO order lists matters in auditor's report; audit committee (Companies Act) oversees financial reporting.

**Likely question angles:** (1) Compute current/quick/GP/debt-equity ratio. (2) Convert GP on cost to GP on sales. (3) Classify a cash transaction into operating, investing, financing. (4) Effect of change in working capital item on cash from operations. (5) BEP and margin of safety numericals. (6) Prime cost, factory cost, cost of production. (7) Labour/material variances. (8) Difference between cost, financial and management accounting. (9) Vouching vs verification; types of audit. (10) Who frames auditing standards / to whom auditor reports.

topics.title: 8. Economics: Introduction, Demand & Macroeconomics
topics.theory:
- **Business (managerial) economics** = application of economic theory to business decision-making; a business economist forecasts, informs management and studies internal/external factors.
- **Law of demand:** price up -> quantity demanded down (other things equal); demand curve slopes downward. Exceptions: **Giffen goods**, Veblen goods.
- **Utility:** Cardinal (Marshall, Gossen), Ordinal (Hicks-Allen), Revealed preference (**Samuelson**). **Total utility is maximum when MU = 0**.
- **Law of equi-marginal utility:** MUx/Px = MUy/Py. **Consumer surplus** (Marshall) = price willing to pay - price actually paid.
- **Elasticity:** Ed = %change Q / %change P; perfectly elastic = infinity, perfectly inelastic = 0; **rectangular hyperbola -> Ed = 1** throughout. Cross elasticity: substitutes (+), **complements (-)**.
- **Income effect:** for an **inferior good**, demand falls as income rises.
- **Keynes:** C = a + bY; **MPC = DC/DY**; MPC + MPS = 1; APC + APS = 1; multiplier = 1/(1 - MPC) = 1/MPS.
- **MEC** (Keynes) vs interest rate decides investment; gross investment - depreciation = net investment.
- **Business cycle** phases: expansion/boom, peak, contraction/depression, trough, recovery. Great Depression began 1929; the earliest global depression = **Long Depression of 1873**.
- **Price floor** binding -> surplus; **price ceiling** binding -> shortage.
- **Macroeconomics** = income and employment theory. PPC shows combinations of two goods producible with given resources.

qs.stem: Which law states that ‘when the price of a product increases, the demand for the same product will fall’?

opts.D: The law of demand

qs.sol: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises.
qs.rel: Law of demand: other things equal, price up means quantity demanded down. Neighbours: Giffen exception, shift vs movement, elasticity.

qs.stem: _____ is a discipline which deals with the application of economic theory to business management.

opts.D: Information processing

qs.sol: Business economics applies economic theory and tools to business-management decision making.
qs.rel: Business (managerial) economics applies economic theory to business decisions. Neighbours: micro vs macro, forecasting, role of business economist.

qs.stem: As the income of the consumer increases, the _____.

opts.A: demand for a normal good becomes zero
opts.B: demand for an inferior good falls
opts.C: demand for an inferior good rises
opts.D: demand for a normal good falls

qs.sol: An inferior good has demand that falls when consumer income rises, because consumers shift to preferred substitutes.
qs.rel: Inferior good: demand falls as income rises; normal good: rises. Neighbours: income elasticity, Giffen good.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are responsibilities of a Business Economist?
 Responsibilities:
 i) Make a reasonable profit on capital employed.
 ii) Make successful forecasts by making in-depth study of the internal and external factors.
 iii) Inform the management of all the economic trends.
 iv) Establish and maintain contacts with individuals and data sources.
 v) Test and analyse the software.

opts.C: i, ii, iii and iv only
opts.D: i, iii and v only

qs.sol: A business economist studies internal and external factors, makes forecasts, informs management about economic trends, and helps the business earn reasonable profit. Testing and analysing software is not a business economist's responsibility. Hence i, ii, iii and iv only are correct.
qs.rel: A business economist forecasts, informs management and studies internal and external factors. Neighbours: managerial economics scope, demand forecasting.

qs.stem: प्रथम वैश्विक आर्थिक मंदी _______ में हुई थी।
qs.sol: यह प्रश्न उन्नीसवीं शताब्दी की दीर्घ मंदी के आरंभ के बारे में है। यूरोप में वियना शेयर बाजार के संकट और उसके बाद अन्य औद्योगिक अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में फैलने वाली वित्तीय कठिनाइयों का आरंभ 1873 में माना जाता है। इसे बीसवीं शताब्दी की महामंदी से नहीं मिलाना चाहिए। दिए गए वर्षों में वैश्विक स्तर पर फैले प्रारंभिक आर्थिक संकट से जुड़ा वर्ष ही उत्तर है।
qs.rel: The first global depression was the Long Depression starting 1873; the Great Depression began 1929. Neighbours: business cycle phases.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not the problem of human capital formation?

opts.A: Rising population is one of the main problems of human capital formation in India
opts.B: Brain drain is one of the main problems of human capital formation in India
opts.C: Low academic standards are another problem of human capital formation in India
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

Rapid population growth stretches education and health resources. Brain drain reduces the domestic return on investment in skilled people. Low academic standards weaken workforce capability. All listed conditions can obstruct human capital formation, so none is an exception.

qs.stem: When the demand curve is straight the point elasticity found ed = 1

opts.A: when the point will be above the midpoint
opts.B: when the point will be below the midpoint of the demand curve
opts.C: when the point will be the mid of the demand curve
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: For a straight-line demand curve meeting both axes, point elasticity equals the ratio of the lower segment to the upper segment measured along the line. At its midpoint, those segments are equal, giving unit elasticity. Above it elasticity is greater than one; below it, less than one.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the unemployment in the rural sector of India?

opts.A: Structural unemployment is a common form of unemployment in rural India
opts.B: Disguised unemployment is a common form of unemployment in rural India
opts.C: Educated unemployment is a common form of unemployment in rural India
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Disguised unemployment is common in rural agriculture: more workers may be engaged than are needed, so some have near-zero marginal productivity. Educated unemployment is more associated with urban job seekers. Structural unemployment can occur but is not the characteristic rural form intended here.

qs.stem: Which of the following programs was initiated by the Government of India to improve the food and nutritional levels of the poor in the country?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The midday meal programme supplies schoolchildren with meals. Integrated Child Development Services provides supplementary nutrition to young children and mothers. The public distribution system makes basic food grains accessible to eligible households. Each contributes to food or nutritional support for poorer groups.

qs.stem: “The excess of the price which he would be willing to pay rather than go without thing, over which he actually does pay, is the economic measure of the surplus satisfaction. It may be called the consumer’s surplus.” This definition is given by

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Consumer surplus is the difference between the maximum amount a buyer would willingly pay and the amount actually paid. The quoted formulation appears in Marshall’s account of consumer surplus. It measures the extra satisfaction in money terms.

qs.stem: Consumption is not only the starting point but the final point of economic activities. Therefore, the true process of economic activities is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A felt want motivates economic activity. Activity organizes resources into production, and the resulting goods or services are consumed to satisfy that want. Consumption then generates further wants, but the requested one-pass sequence ends with consumption.

qs.stem: The concept of consumer surplus depends on

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Consumer surplus is the excess of willingness to pay over the actual price paid. Diminishing marginal utility makes earlier units worth more to the buyer than later units. Paying a common market price therefore leaves surplus on the earlier units.

qs.stem: The theory of cross elasticity of demand is depicted by

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Cross elasticity measures how the demand for one good responds to a change in another good’s price. Henry L. Moore is credited in this exam’s standard history with introducing the cross-elasticity concept. The official key therefore assigns this attribution to Moore.

qs.stem: A classical economist prefers

opts.C: consumption and production both for the good of the nation
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Classical economists emphasized production and capital accumulation as drivers of national wealth. In the classical account, output and productive capacity receive priority over consumption as the central policy concern. The question contrasts that emphasis with consumption-led approaches.

qs.stem: What is true?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Average propensity to consume is C/Y and average propensity to save is S/Y. Since disposable income is allocated to consumption and saving, C + S = Y. Dividing by Y yields APC + APS = 1.

qs.stem: According to Schumpeter, economic equilibrium includes

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Equilibrium can be classified by its response to a small disturbance: return to the original state, movement farther away, or settlement at a new nearby state. These are stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium respectively. Thus several listed forms are included.

qs.stem: Consumer’s equilibrium analysis mainly includes

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Consumer equilibrium is studied by cardinal utility, indifference-curve or ordinal utility, and revealed preference approaches. Each explains how a consumer chooses an attainable bundle, using a different account of preferences. Therefore several listed analyses apply.

qs.stem: The other name of macroeconomics is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Macroeconomics studies aggregate output, national income and economy-wide employment. For this reason it is also called the theory of income and employment. Price theory commonly refers to microeconomics and individual market prices; distribution theory studies the division of income among factors.

qs.stem: Perfectly inelastic demand is equal to

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Price elasticity is percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price. In perfectly inelastic demand the quantity does not change when price changes. The numerator is zero, so elasticity is zero and the demand curve is vertical.

qs.stem: Perfectly elastic demand is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. With perfectly elastic demand, even an arbitrarily small price rise removes demand at the given price. The ratio tends to infinity and the demand curve is horizontal.

qs.stem: With the increase in investment, MEC (Marginal Efficiency of Capital)

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Marginal efficiency of capital is the expected return from an additional unit of investment relative to its supply price. As investment expands, the best opportunities are used first; later projects usually yield less. Thus the marginal efficiency schedule slopes downward.

qs.stem: The degree that an economic variable changes in response to a change in another economic variable is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Elasticity measures how strongly one economic variable responds to a change in another.

It is commonly expressed as percentage change in the dependent variable divided by percentage change in the driver.

That responsiveness is what the stem defines.

qs.stem: Which one among the following is considered as one of the important economic factors which determines entrepreneurial growth?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Market size and demand affect expected sales and profit, so market conditions are an economic determinant of entrepreneurial growth. Government and politics influence policy, but they are not the market factor sought by this classification.

qs.stem: Who among the following described the view that “The desire to save is the cause of unemployment”?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

In Keynesian macroeconomics, total output and employment depend on effective demand, meaning the aggregate spending that firms expect for their goods and services.

When households collectively try to save more without an equal rise in investment, consumption and aggregate demand fall. Firms then reduce production and employment; this is the paradox of thrift.

Application

The statement links a stronger desire to save with unemployment through lower spending and deficient effective demand. The BPSC final answer key for Series A question 103 identifies J. M. Keynes as the person associated with this statement.

Contrast

P. H. …

qs.stem: If the percentage change in demand is –7·5%, and the percentage change in price is 5%, then price elasticity of demand shall be

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Price elasticity of demand is the absolute percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price. Here |−7.5%| ÷ 5% = 1.5; the negative sign records the inverse direction, not the reported magnitude.

qs.stem: The other name of macro-economics is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Macroeconomics studies aggregate output, national income and economy-wide employment. For that reason it is traditionally called the theory of income and employment; individual market prices and factor distribution are narrower subjects.

qs.stem:
Total utility is maximum when
1. Marginal utility is zero.
2. Marginal utility is positive.
3. Marginal utility is negative.
4. When consumer is fully satisfied.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Code:

opts.D: 1 and 4

qs.sol: At the saturation point marginal utility is zero and the consumer is fully satisfied, so statements 1 and 4 describe maximum total utility.

qs.stem: Law of equi marginal utility is based on assumption that purchasing power of money and marginal utility of money remains

opts.D: Variable

qs.sol: Equi-marginal utility assumes the marginal utility of money and its purchasing power remain constant across the allocation.

qs.stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

opts.A: The Marginal Propensity to Consume is higher in case of poor than in that of rich people.
opts.B: Marginal Propensity to Consume is the consumption per unit of income.
opts.C: The Marginal Propensity to Consume is always positive but less than one.
opts.D: In underdeveloped countries, the Marginal Propensity to Consume tends to be high, whereas in advanced countries it tends to be low.

qs.sol:
MPC is Δconsumption/Δincome, the change in consumption divided by a change in income.

Consumption per unit of income instead defines average propensity to consume.

Thus the second statement is the incorrect one.

qs.stem: The Marginal Propensity to Consume is equal to:

opts.C: Change in consumption / Change in income (ΔC/ΔY)
opts.D: Change in consumption / Change in saving (ΔC/ΔS)

qs.sol:
Marginal propensity measures the extra consumption from an extra unit of income.

Taking the change in consumption divided by the change in income gives ΔC/ΔY.

qs.stem: A fall in the price of a commodity, holding everything else constant, results in and is referred to as:

opts.C: an extension in the quantity demanded.
opts.D: a decrease in the quantity demanded.

qs.sol:
Changing only the good's own price moves along the same demand curve.

A lower price raises quantity demanded, which is called an extension in quantity demanded.

qs.stem: If the amount of both commodities (x and y) increase or decrease when the price of one changes, the cross elasticity of demand between them is:

opts.D: one

qs.sol:
The two goods move together in consumption, indicating complementary demand.

For complements, a price rise in one lowers demand for the other, giving a negative cross-price elasticity.

qs.stem: At the point of saturation, total utility of a commodity is –

opts.D: Negative

qs.sol:
Total utility rises as long as marginal utility is positive.

At the saturation point marginal utility becomes zero, so total utility stops rising.

It is therefore at its highest level; beyond it marginal utility turns negative and total utility falls.

qs.stem: Downward movement along the same demand curve shows –

opts.D: Decrease in demand

qs.sol:
A movement along a given demand curve is caused only by a change in the commodity’s own price.

Moving downward means price falls and quantity demanded rises.

A price-induced rise in quantity demanded on the same curve is called expansion of demand.

“1929” इस प्रश्न का सही उत्तर है: 1929 के शेयर बाजार ध्वंस के बाद विश्व महामंदी शुरू हुई। 1942 दूसरे विश्व युद्ध का वर्ष है, आरंभिक आर्थिक ध्वंस का नहीं। “1942” उपयुक्त नहीं है: 1942 तक महामंदी शुरू हो चुकी थी।

qs.stem: In a rectangular hyperbola demand curve, the price elasticity of demand will be :

opts.D: inelastic

qs.sol: A rectangular hyperbola keeps price times quantity constant, so its elasticity is one at every point. “perfectly elastic” would be a horizontal demand line, while “perfectly inelastic” would be vertical.

qs.stem: Correct formula of Cross elasticity of demand is :

opts.D: ΔQx/ΔPx × Qx/Py

qs.sol: Cross elasticity compares the proportionate change in quantity of X with the proportionate change in price of Y, giving “ΔQx/ΔPy × Py/Qx”. “ΔQx/ΔPx × Py/Qx” uses the price change of X and cannot measure a cross-price response.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are correct regarding cardinal utility analysis ?

(A) The marginal utility diminishes with increase in consumption of a commodity.

(B) Marginal utility can not be negative

opts.D: Both (A) and (B) are incorrect

qs.sol: Diminishing marginal utility says extra utility normally falls as consumption rises, making “Only (A) is correct” apt. Marginal utility can become negative after satiation, so “Both (A) and (B) are correct” fails.

qs.stem: A binding floor price leads to :

opts.D: Shortage of supply

qs.sol: A binding floor lies above equilibrium, so producers offer more than buyers demand: “Excess supply”. “Excess demand” instead follows a binding ceiling below equilibrium.

qs.stem: If Price Ceiling is binding in wheat market, it will lead to a situation of :

opts.D: Excess supply

qs.sol: A binding ceiling is below equilibrium; buyers demand more wheat than sellers supply, creating “Excess demand”. “Excess supply” is associated with a binding floor.

qs.stem:
Given the following demand and supply equations :

Qd = 1200−P

Qs = 900+ 2P

What will be equilibrium price ?
qs.sol: Set demand equal to supply: 1200−P = 900+2P, so 3P=300 and P=100. “300” is the price difference before division by three, not the equilibrium price.

qs.stem: If the total expenditure on a good and its price move in opposite direction, the price elasticity will be :

opts.D: Zero

qs.sol: When price falls and total expenditure rises, the quantity response is proportionately larger than the price change: elasticity is “More than 1”. With “Equal to1”, total expenditure stays unchanged.

qs.stem: The shape of unitary elastic demand curve will be :

opts.D: Linear

qs.sol: A rectangular hyperbola has constant P×Q, hence unit elasticity throughout. “Horizontal” depicts perfectly elastic demand, not unit elasticity.

qs.stem: Which of the following is true in case of Giffen goods ?

opts.D: Income and substitution effect work in same direction.

qs.sol: The negative income effect for a Giffen good outweighs the substitution effect, so “Income effect > Substitution effect” in magnitude. “Substitution effect > Income effect” would preserve ordinary downward-sloping demand.

qs.stem: The demand for a good and the price of its complementary goods will be related.

opts.D: Positively and proportionally

qs.sol: A higher complement price reduces joint use and lowers demand for the good, so the relation is “Negatively”. “Positively” describes substitutes, not complements.

qs.stem: Suppose X and Y are substitute goods and if Price of Y increases, the demand curve of X will :

opts.D: Indeterminate

qs.sol: A rise in the price of substitute Y sends consumers toward X, so X demand will “Shift rightward”. “Shift leftward” would imply reduced demand for X.
At P>15 both linear expressions are negative, and feasible demand cannot be below zero; thus both demand “0 and 0”. “5 and 0” cannot follow from dA=10−P at such a price.
With an upward-sloping supply curve, a rightward demand shift raises both equilibrium quantity and price, so “increase and increase” is correct. “increase and decrease” reverses the price response.
The elasticity magnitude is 15%/25%=0.6, hence “Less than 1”. “More than 1” would require a proportionately larger quantity change than the price change.

qs.stem: Suppose market price of a commodity increases from Rs. 5 to Rs. 20. As a result quantity supplied by a firm increases by 15 units. The price elasticity of supply is 0.5. What is the initial output of this firm ?
qs.sol: Using the initial-value elasticity formula, 0.5=(15/Q)/(15/5)=5/Q, giving Q=10. “15” is the change in quantity, not initial output.

qs.stem:
Investment demand in an economy depends on :

(A) Marginal propensity to consume

(B) Marginal efficiency of capital

(C) Rate of interest

opts.D: All (A), (B) and (C)

qs.sol: The printed answer “Only (B) and (C)” is supported: Only (B) and (C) directly determine planned investment through expected return on capital compared with financing cost. The alternative “Only (A) and (B)” fails: Marginal propensity to consume affects consumption and the multiplier, not the direct investment decision. No official final key was published; answer verified by our review.

qs.stem: Production Possibility Frontier curve shows a combination of goods that :

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “an economy can produce” is the official answer because A PPF describes technically feasible production combinations for the economy. “a producer wants to produce” fails because a producer’s wishes do not establish the economy-wide feasibility frontier.

qs.stem: Cardinal utility analysis assumes that:

opts.A: Level of utility can be expressed in numbers
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “More than one of the above” is the official answer because “Level of utility can be expressed in numbers” and “Utility is subjective” both qualify: Cardinal utility treats utility as measurable numerically; Utility is experienced subjectively by the consumer. “Consumer ranks various consumption bundles” fails because ranking bundles is the ordinal rather than cardinal method.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct about elasticity of demand

opts.A: It is percentage change in demand for the good divided by percentage change in its price
opts.B: Elasticity of demand is same at different points on a linear demand curve
opts.C: Elasticity of demand of necessity goods is highly elastic
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “It is percentage change in demand for the good divided by percentage change in its price” is the official answer because Price elasticity compares percentage quantity-demanded change with percentage price change. “Elasticity of demand is same at different points on a linear demand curve” fails because point elasticity varies along an ordinary straight-line demand curve.

qs.stem: In the simple keynesian model, consumption is a function of:

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Level of income” is the official answer because The simple Keynesian consumption function relates consumption to current income. “Rate of interest” fails because interest rates are not its direct explanatory variable in the simple model.

qs.stem: The difference between gross investment and net investment is:

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Depreciation” is the official answer because Gross investment less capital consumption equals net investment. “Multiplier” fails because the multiplier is a spending-response ratio, not the gap between investment measures.

qs.stem: Consumer behaviour is studied in :

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Micro Economics” is the official answer because Microeconomics examines individual consumers and firms. “Macro Economics” fails because macroeconomics studies aggregate output, employment and prices.

qs.stem: Which of the following denotes business activity at high level with increasing output and income?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Boom” is selected because a boom is the high activity phase with rising output and income. “Recession” fails because a recession contracts rather than expands activity.

qs.stem: The slope of production possibility curve is

opts.A: concave to the point of origin
opts.B: convex to the point of origin
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “concave to the point of origin” describes the usual bowed-out production possibility frontier. “convex to the point of origin” would imply a different curvature from the usual frontier.

qs.stem: If the consumer income declines, then the demand for

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “inferior goods will increase” is correct: inferior-good demand rises as income falls. “normal goods will increase” is wrong here: normal-good demand generally falls with lower income.

qs.stem: The elasticity coefficient for perfectly elastic demand curve is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “infinity” is correct: infinite elasticity describes a horizontal demand curve. “one” is wrong here: one denotes unit elasticity.

qs.stem: Who basically propounded the concept of law of equi-marginal utility?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Gossen” is credited with Gossen's second law, the equi-marginal principle. “J. S. Mill” is not credited with the original law of equi-marginal utility.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a determinant of supply?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Demonstration effect” affects consumption behavior rather than a producer's supply decision. “Expectations about future prices” is wrong here: future expected prices can alter present supply.

qs.stem: Who propounded psychological law of consumption?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

उत्पादन संभावना वक्र तब बाहर की ओर खिसकता है जब अर्थव्यवस्था की उत्पादन क्षमता बढ़ती है। आर्थिक विकास, उत्पादक संसाधनों में वृद्धि और प्रौद्योगिकी में सुधार इस क्षमता को बढ़ाते हैं। इसलिए उत्तर है: उपर्युक्त सभी।
मांग के निर्धारक वस्तु की कीमत, संबंधित वस्तुओं की कीमत और उपभोक्ता की आय जैसे आर्थिक कारक होते हैं। दिए गए विकल्पों में सरकार का प्रकार मांग का निर्धारक नहीं है।

मांग का नियम सीमांत उपयोगिता क्षीणता के नियम पर आधारित है। जैसे-जैसे उपभोक्ता किसी वस्तु की अधिक इकाइयाँ प्राप्त करता है, प्रत्येक अतिरिक्त इकाई से मिलने वाली उपयोगिता घटती जाती है। इसलिए वह अधिक मात्रा तभी खरीदेगा जब कीमत कम हो, जिससे मांग वक्र दायीं ओर नीचे की ओर ढलता है। अतः उत्तर: सीमांत उपयोगिता क्षीणता का नियम।
सीमांत उपयोगिता ह्रास नियम के अनुसार, जब सीमांत उपयोगिता शून्य हो जाती है, तब कुल उपयोगिता अपनी अधिकतम सीमा पर पहुँचती है। इसलिए उत्तर है: अधिकतम।
आपूर्ति के नियम के अनुसार, अन्य बातें समान रहने पर वस्तु का मूल्य बढ़ने से उसकी आपूर्ति बढ़ती है और मूल्य घटने से आपूर्ति घटती है। इसलिए आपूर्ति वक्र दाहिनी ओर ऊपर की ओर ढलान वाला होता है।

कीनेसियन आय निर्धारण के सरल सिद्धांत में निवेश को स्वायत्त माना जाता है, यानी उसका स्तर आय से स्वतंत्र और मॉडल के बाहर निर्धारित होता है।

इसलिए आय में परिवर्तन होने पर निवेश स्वतः नहीं बदलता। यहाँ निवेश बहिर्जात है।

पूंजी की सीमांत दक्षता अनुसूची में आवक परिवर्तन का अर्थ है कि प्रत्येक ब्याज दर पर अपेक्षित लाभप्रदता और निवेश घट जाता है। निवेश समग्र मांग का एक घटक है। इसलिए निवेश में कमी से समग्र मांग में कमी होगी।
एक पूरा चक्र चार चरणों में सम्पन्न होता है। इसलिए उत्तर है: चार चरण।

qs.stem: The law of demand states that if other things remain same

opts.A: There is always a direct relationship between the price and demand
opts.B: There is always an inverse relationship between price and demand
opts.C: There is always a direct relationship between desire and demand
opts.D: There is no relationship between price and demand

qs.sol: The law of demand states that, with other factors unchanged, price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions. Therefore, as price rises demand falls, and as price falls demand rises: There is always an inverse relationship between price and demand.

qs.stem: With regard to business cycles which of the following is not true ?

opts.A: Expansion, recession, depression and recovery are the four phases of business cycles
opts.B: Business cycle is a part of the capitalist system

opts.D: The innovations theory of business cycle is associated with the name of Joseph Schumpeter

qs.sol: Keynes did not consider the trade cycle a purely monetary phenomenon; he linked it mainly to fluctuations in investment and the marginal efficiency of capital. Therefore, the statement “According to Keynes, ‘The trade cycle is a purely monetary phenomenon’” is not true.

qs.stem: According to Marshall the basis of consumer surplus is

opts.D: Law of variable proportions

qs.sol: The basis of consumer surplus is the law of diminishing marginal utility: as a consumer buys more units of a commodity, the marginal utility from each successive unit decreases. Therefore, the consumer is willing to pay more for earlier units than for later ones, creating a surplus when the market price is uniform. Hence, the answer is Law of diminishing marginal utility.
