qs.stem: The per day calorie estimate of poverty for rural economies is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
India’s traditional calorie-based poverty criterion uses a minimum daily intake of 2400 calories per person in rural areas.

A rural person consuming less than this benchmark falls below the calorie-based poverty threshold. Hence, the answer is less than 2400.

qs.stem: Production Possibility Curve will be a straight line if

opts.D: None of these

qs.sol:
The slope of a Production Possibility Curve reflects marginal opportunity cost—the amount of one good sacrificed to produce an additional unit of another.

A straight line has a constant slope, so the sacrifice per additional unit remains unchanged. Hence, the curve is a straight line when marginal opportunity cost is constant.

qs.stem: According to whom , “production possibility curve is the curve which depicts all the combinations of such goods and services whose maximum amount can be produced with the help of all the available factors and technology in the condition of full employment of factors.”

opts.D: David Ricardo

qs.sol:
A production possibility curve shows the maximum attainable combinations of goods and services when available resources are fully employed, given the existing technology.

The quoted definition expresses this idea and is attributed to P. Samuelson.

qs.stem: the relationship between quantity demanded and price of a commodity is explained by

opts.D: Law of production

qs.sol:
The law of demand explains the relationship between a commodity’s price and the quantity demanded, other things remaining constant.

As price rises, quantity demanded falls; as price falls, quantity demanded rises. Hence, the answer is Law of demand.

qs.stem: The relationship between price and quantity demanded is

opts.D: All of these

qs.sol:
The law of demand states that, other things remaining constant, price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

As price rises, quantity demanded falls; as price falls, quantity demanded rises. Hence, the relationship is Inverse.

qs.stem: the elasticity of demand for necessary goods is

opts.D: None of these

qs.sol:
Price elasticity of demand measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in price.

Necessary goods are essential, so their demand changes proportionately less than their price. Their demand is therefore inelastic, with elasticity less than one in magnitude.

Answer: less than one.

qs.stem: Cardinal marginal utility approach assumes

opts.B: constancy of marginal utility of money
opts.D: All of these

qs.sol:
The cardinal marginal utility approach treats utility as numerically measurable. It assumes:

Cardinal measurability of utility: satisfaction can be expressed in numerical units.

Constancy of marginal utility of money: the utility of an additional unit of money remains constant.

Independence of utilities: utility from one good depends only on its own consumption.

All three are assumptions, so the answer is All of these.

qs.stem: As per the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, when Marginal utility is zero, total utility is

opts.D: increasing

qs.sol:
Marginal utility is the additional utility gained from consuming one more unit. Under the law of diminishing marginal utility, it falls as consumption increases.

When marginal utility reaches zero, total utility stops increasing and reaches its maximum. Beyond this point, negative marginal utility reduces total utility.

Answer: maximum.

qs.stem: A decrease in marginal propensity to consume will –

opts.A: Decrease the overall aggregate demand of the economy
opts.B: Lead to decrease in the equilibrium level of income or output
opts.C: "Decrease the overall aggregate demand of the economy" and "Lead to decrease in the equilibrium level of income or output" both
opts.D: Neither "Decrease the overall aggregate demand of the economy " nor "Lead to decrease in the equilibrium level of income or output"

qs.sol:
Marginal propensity to consume is the share of additional income spent on consumption.

When it decreases, consumption spending falls at a given positive income, other things unchanged. This reduces aggregate demand.

Lower aggregate demand leads firms to reduce production, lowering equilibrium income or output.

Thus, both a decrease in overall aggregate demand and a decrease in equilibrium income or output occur.

qs.stem: An inward shift in the Marginal Efficiency of Capital schedule would –

opts.D: Accelerate Economic Growth

qs.sol:
The Marginal Efficiency of Capital schedule shows the expected return on additional investment. An inward shift means lower expected returns, so firms invest less at a given interest rate.

Investment is a component of aggregate demand. Therefore, lower investment will Decrease Aggregate Demand.

qs.stem: If marginal utility is zero then

opts.B: An additional unit of consumption will decrease total utility
opts.C: An additional unit of consumption will increase total utility
opts.D: Total utility is maximised

qs.sol:
Marginal utility is the additional satisfaction gained from consuming one more unit. Under diminishing marginal utility, total utility rises while marginal utility is positive and falls when it becomes negative.

When marginal utility is zero, total utility stops rising and reaches its maximum. Hence, total utility is maximised.

qs.stem: Which is not the part of business cycle ?

opts.D: Acceleration

qs.sol:
The business cycle consists of recurring phases such as boom, recession, depression and recovery.

Boom, Depression and Recovery are therefore parts of the business cycle. Acceleration is not a standard phase.

Answer: Acceleration.

qs.stem: The subject matter of Macro Economics includes

opts.D: All of the above

qs.sol:
Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole, including aggregate income, international economic relations and economic fluctuations.

National income measures total income; international trade concerns trade between countries; and trade cycles are economy-wide fluctuations in activity. All three fall within macroeconomics.

Therefore, the answer is All of the above.

qs.stem:
“The Demand for anything at a given price is the amount of it, which will be bought per unit of time at that price.”
Above definition of Demand is given by -

opts.D: Bober

qs.sol:
Demand at a given price is the quantity that buyers will purchase per unit of time at that price.

The quoted definition is attributed to **Benham**, who explicitly links demand to both price and a specified time period.

topics.deep:
- **Scope:** Business (managerial) economics applies microeconomic tools to business decisions - demand analysis and forecasting, cost, pricing, profit, capital budgeting. Micro = individual units; Macro = aggregates (income, employment, prices). Basic problem: scarcity -> choice -> opportunity cost.
- **Production possibility curve (PPC):** shows maximum combinations of two goods with given resources and technology; concave to origin because of increasing opportunity cost (straight line if constant); slope = marginal rate of transformation; outward shift = growth.
- **Utility analysis:**
| Approach | Idea | Proponents |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal | Utility measurable in utils | Marshall, Gossen, Jevons |
| Ordinal / IC | Ranking, indifference curves | Hicks and Allen |
| Revealed preference | Choice reveals preference | Samuelson |
- **Law of diminishing marginal utility:** as consumption rises, MU falls; TU rises at a decreasing rate; **TU max when MU = 0** (point of satiety); beyond it MU is negative. **Equi-marginal law:** MUx/Px = MUy/Py = MU of money (Marshall assumes MU of money constant). **Consumer surplus** = total utility - price x quantity; example: willing to pay 100, pays 70, surplus = 30.
- **Indifference curve:** downward sloping, convex to origin (diminishing MRS), non-intersecting; equilibrium at tangency with budget line: MRS = Px/Py.
- **Demand:** determinants - price, income, tastes, price of related goods, expectations. Movement along the curve = price change (expansion/contraction); shift = other determinants (increase/decrease). Exceptions: Giffen goods (strongly inferior; demand falls when price falls), Veblen goods, speculative demand. Complementary goods: price of complement up -> demand for the good down; substitutes: price of Y rises -> demand for X rises (shift right).
- **Elasticity:**
| Type | Ed | Total expenditure on price rise |
|---|---|---|
| Perfectly elastic | infinity | - |
| Elastic | > 1 | Falls |
| Unitary | = 1 | Unchanged (rectangular hyperbola) |
| Inelastic | < 1 | Rises |
| Perfectly inelastic | 0 | Rises proportionally |
Income elasticity: positive for normal goods, negative for inferior goods, above 1 for luxuries. Cross elasticity: +ve substitutes, -ve complements; formula = %change in Qx / %change in Py. Examples: Q from 100 to 120 when P from 10 to 8: Ed = 20%/20% = 1. Percentage change in demand -7.5% for 5% price change: Ed = 1.5.
- **Market equilibrium:** Qd = Qs. Qd = 1200 - P, Qs = 900 + 2P -> 300 = 3P -> P = 100, Q = 1100. **Price ceiling** below equilibrium -> shortage (rationing); **price floor** above equilibrium -> surplus.
- **Macro - Keynes:** C = a + bY; **MPC = DC/DY**; APC = C/Y; MPC + MPS = 1; APC + APS = 1; if MPS = 0, MPC = 1; **multiplier k = 1/(1 - MPC)** (MPC 0.8 -> k = 5). Psychological law of consumption: as income rises consumption rises by less. Fall in MPC lowers the multiplier. Investment: depends on **MEC** (marginal efficiency of capital) and rate of interest; inward shift of MEC schedule reduces investment and income; gross - depreciation = net investment.
- **Income and employment:** Unemployment types - frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal, disguised (common in Indian agriculture). Keynes explained involuntary unemployment by deficient effective demand (paradox of thrift: saving by all reduces income). Poverty line (Planning Commission): rural 2400 kcal/day, urban 2100 kcal. Human capital formation: investment in education/health; problems - brain drain, low quality.
- **Business cycle:** phases: expansion (boom), peak, contraction (recession/depression), trough, recovery. Samuelson's multiplier-accelerator model gives regular cycles for certain parameter values. First global depression: Long Depression from 1873 (Vienna crash); Great Depression began 1929.
- **Supply:** law - price up, supply up; determinants - input prices, technology, taxes, number of firms. Not a determinant of supply: consumer income.

**Likely question angles:** (1) Define business economics/macro. (2) Law of demand; exceptions. (3) Elasticity numericals and total-expenditure method. (4) Cross-elasticity of complements/substitutes. (5) TU/MU relationship. (6) Equi-marginal law formula. (7) MPC/APC identities and multiplier. (8) Effect of price ceiling/floor. (9) Match utility approaches with authors. (10) Business cycle phases and causes.

topics.title: 9. Production, Costs & Market Forms
topics.theory:
- **Production function:** Q = f(inputs); short run (one input fixed) vs long run (all variable).
- **Law of variable proportions:** Stage I increasing returns, **Stage II diminishing returns (rational stage)**, Stage III negative returns (MP < 0, TP falls). TP rises while MP is positive; TP maximum at MP = 0.
- **Isoquant:** all input combinations giving same output; convex, downward sloping; **MRTS = MPL/MPK** = slope. **Isocost** = same total cost; producer equilibrium at tangency (least-cost combination).
- **Technical efficiency** = maximum output from given physical inputs; economic efficiency = least cost.
- **Costs:** TC = TFC + TVC; AFC is a rectangular hyperbola; **SMC, SAC and AVC are U-shaped**; MC cuts AC at its minimum.
- **LAC** is U-shaped/saucer due to economies then diseconomies of scale.
- **Perfect competition:** many sellers, homogeneous product, price taker, **P = MR = AR**; equilibrium MC = MR.
- **Monopoly:** single seller, AR > MR; **price discrimination** when elasticity differs, with lower price where elasticity is higher.
- **Monopolistic competition** (Chamberlin): many sellers, differentiated product, downward-sloping demand, normal profit in long run, excess capacity.
- **Oligopoly:** few sellers, interdependence, kinked demand curve. **Natural monopoly:** utilities with declining long-run costs.

qs.stem: Short run marginal cost curve is _____.

opts.D: Inverse U-shaped

qs.sol:
The shape of a short-run cost curve is governed by the law of variable proportions (diminishing marginal returns): with at least one fixed factor in the short run, adding more of the variable factor first raises output at an increasing rate, then — beyond a point — at a decreasing rate. Marginal cost (MC), being the change in total cost per additional unit of output, mirrors this pattern inversely: it falls while returns are increasing and rises once diminishing returns set in.

Applying this to the short-run MC curve: in the early stage of production, better utilisation of the fixed factor lets output rise faster than cost, so MC declines. …
qs.rel: SMC is U-shaped due to the law of variable proportions and cuts AC and AVC at their minimum. Neighbours: LAC saucer shape, AFC hyperbola.

qs.stem:
In the context of production theory, what does the term ‘marginal rate of technical

substitution’ (MRTS) measure?

opts.A: The rate at which total cost increases as output expands
opts.B: The rate at which marginal cost decreases with an increase in output
opts.C: The rate at which a firm can substitute between two inputs while keeping output constant
opts.D: The rate at which average variable cost varies with changes in fixed inputs

qs.sol:
In production theory, an isoquant is the curve showing every combination of two inputs — typically labour (L) and capital (K) — that yields the same level of output. The Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution (MRTS) is defined as the rate at which one input can be substituted for the other along a given isoquant while total output stays exactly constant: MRTS(L for K) = -ΔK/ΔL = MPL/MPK, the ratio of the two inputs' marginal products, which equals the absolute value of the isoquant's slope at that point (the isoquant itself slopes downward, with slope equal to -MRTS).

Applying this to the item: the question asks precisely what MRTS measures. …
qs.rel: MRTS is the rate at which one input substitutes for another keeping output constant; slope of isoquant (MPL/MPK). Neighbours: isocost, producer equilibrium.

qs.stem: उत्पादन विश्लेषण में ‘आगतों के न्यूनतम लागत संयोग’ अवधारणा का उपयोग करने का उद्देश्य क्या है?

opts.A: उत्पादन से उत्पन्न कुल राजस्व को अधिकतम करना
opts.B: उत्पादन के किसी निश्चित स्तर के लिए कुल लागत को न्यूनतम करना
opts.C: परिवर्तनीय लागतों को कम करके लाभ मार्जिन को अनुकूलित करना
opts.D: उत्पादन में वृद्धि के माध्यम से पैमाने की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं को अधिकतम करना

qs.sol:
संकल्पना

न्यूनतम-लागत संयोग प्रतिस्थापनीय आगतों का ऐसा समूह है, जो न्यूनतम संभव कुल आगत लागत पर उत्पादन का एक निर्दिष्ट स्तर उत्पन्न करता है।

आंतरिक अनुकूलतम बिंदु पर समोत्पाद वक्र की ढाल समलागत रेखा की ढाल के बराबर होती है: सीमांत तकनीकी प्रतिस्थापन दर आगत कीमतों के अनुपात के बराबर होती है।

अनुप्रयोग

यहाँ उत्पादन स्तर को स्थिर रखा गया है। उत्पादक उसी समोत्पाद वक्र पर स्थित व्यवहार्य आगत समूहों की तुलना करता है और न्यूनतम प्राप्य समलागत रेखा पर स्थित समूह का चयन करता है, जिससे उस उत्पादन की कुल उत्पादन लागत न्यूनतम हो जाती है।

तुलना

कुल आगम का अधिकतमीकरण कीमत और बेची गई मात्रा से संबंधित है, न कि स्थिर उत्पादन के लिए आगतों के लागत-न्यूनकारी मिश्रण से।

लाभ मार्जिन का अनुकूलन आगम और लाग …
qs.rel: Least-cost combination: producing a given output at minimum total input cost (isoquant tangent to isocost). Neighbours: MRTS, economic efficiency.

qs.stem: अल्पकाल में, यदि अन्य सभी आगतों को स्थिर रखते हुए केवल एक परिवर्ती आगत की मात्रा में वृद्धि की जाए और उस आगत का सीमांत उत्पाद धनात्मक बना रहे, तो उत्पादन फलन के अनुसार कुल निर्गत पर इसका क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा?

opts.D: आगत और निर्गत के बीच कोई संबंध नहीं है।

qs.sol:
उत्पादन फलन (Production Function) वह तकनीकी संबंध है जो किसी वस्तु के उत्पादन में प्रयुक्त आगतों (जैसे श्रम, पूँजी) की मात्रा को उससे प्राप्त अधिकतम संभव निर्गत (उत्पादन) से जोड़ता है। अल्पकाल में जब कुछ आगत (जैसे पूँजी) स्थिर रखे जाते हैं और केवल एक परिवर्ती आगत (जैसे श्रम) की मात्रा बदली जाती है, तो निर्गत में होने वाला परिवर्तन परिवर्ती अनुपात के नियम (Law of Variable Proportions) से निर्धारित होता है।

इस नियम के अनुसार, जब तक अतिरिक्त इकाई आगत का सीमांत उत्पाद (Marginal Product) धनात्मक रहता है, तब तक परिवर्ती आगत में वृद्धि से कुल निर्गत (Total Product) भी बढ़ता है — भले ही वृद्धि की दर पहले बढ़े (सीमांत प्रतिफल वृद्धि की अवस्था) और फिर घटे (सीमांत प्रतिफल ह्रास की अवस्था), कुल निर्गत  …
qs.rel: With positive marginal product, total product rises (at a decreasing rate in stage II). Neighbours: TP max at MP = 0, law of variable proportions.

qs.stem: What is 'technical efficiency' in production theory concerned with?

opts.A: Maximising output by employing the least-cost combination of inputs
opts.B: Minimising fixed costs through optimal resource allocation
opts.C: Achieving the highest possible profit margins from production
opts.D: Minimising wastage of inputs to produce a given level of output

qs.sol: In production theory, efficiency is analysed along two independent dimensions. Technical efficiency is a purely physical (engineering) criterion: an input-output combination is technically efficient when no input can be reduced without reducing output -- equivalently, there is no wastage of inputs for a given output level. It depends only on the production function/isoquant, never on input or output prices. Allocative (economic) efficiency is a separate, additional requirement: among all technically efficient combinations, it selects the one that minimises cost given the relative prices of the inputs. …
qs.rel: Technical efficiency concerns getting maximum physical output from given inputs; economic efficiency adds cost minimisation. Neighbours: isoquants.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding monopolistic competition?

opts.A: The marginal revenue is slightly less than the average revenue
opts.B: The goods produced by them are not homogeneous
opts.C: The demand curve faced by the firm is horizontal
opts.D: The market structure of the firm allows for new firms to enter the market

qs.sol: In monopolistic competition, firms face a downward-sloping demand curve because products are differentiated. A horizontal demand curve is a feature of perfect competition, so that statement is not correct here.
qs.rel: Monopolistic competition has differentiated products and a downward-sloping demand curve, so a horizontal demand curve is wrong. Neighbours: normal profit, excess capacity.

qs.stem: “Perfect competition prevails when the demand for the output of each producer is perfectly elastic. This entails first, the number of sellers is large so that output of any one seller is negligible small production of the total output of the commodity and second that buyers are all alike in respect of their choice between rival sellers, so that the market is perfect.” Who gave the definition?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The quotation defines perfect competition through perfectly elastic demand for each producer and many negligible sellers. This wording is attributed to Joan Robinson in the standard account of imperfect competition. The buyers’ indifference among sellers explains why any one seller faces a horizontal demand curve.

qs.stem: Monopolistic firm will be in equilibrium when

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A firm with market power faces downward-sloping demand, so price exceeds marginal revenue at positive output. Profit maximization sets marginal revenue equal to marginal cost, assuming an interior optimum. Combining these gives price above their common value.

qs.stem: Under discriminating monopoly, when elasticity of demand is greater, monopolist will keep his price

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: At an optimum with price discrimination, marginal revenue is equalized across the separated markets. For the same marginal cost, the inverse-elasticity rule gives a smaller markup where demand is more elastic. Hence the seller charges a lower price in that market.

qs.stem: Under discriminating monopoly, there will be equilibrium when

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: In two segmented markets, profit is maximized by allocating output until the marginal revenue earned in each market is equal. Total output is then chosen where that common marginal revenue equals marginal cost. Equalizing the two marginal revenues alone leaves total output undetermined.

qs.stem: Which statement is true? In monopolistic competition

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the Hindi printing omitted the AR < MR choice, so its translation was restored from the English column. A firm in monopolistic competition faces downward-sloping demand because its product is differentiated. Selling an extra unit generally requires a lower price, so marginal revenue lies below average revenue.

qs.stem: In perfect competition, firms are

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A perfectly competitive firm is too small to influence the market price. Many sellers supply a homogeneous product, so an individual firm faces a horizontal demand curve at the given price. It accepts that price and chooses its output.

qs.stem: “The act of selling the same article produced under a single control, at different prices to different buyers is known as price discrimination.” Who has given this definition?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Price discrimination charges different buyers different prices for the same product under one seller’s control. The quoted wording is attributed to Joan Robinson in the standard account of imperfect competition. It identifies the sale under single control rather than a difference in production cost.

qs.stem: Law of diminishing return is found

opts.C: in some extent it applies in every economic activities
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Diminishing returns arise when one input is increased while other inputs remain fixed. Beyond a point, each extra unit of the variable input adds less output. This short-run mechanism can occur in agriculture, manufacturing, or services.

qs.stem: Under monopolistic competition

opts.A: firms do not depend on industry
opts.B: price determined by industry is given to all the firms
opts.C: firms and industry are unrelated to each other
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

Modified from the official paper: the vague statement that firms and industry are “different” could be read as true; it now says they are unrelated, which is false. Firms collectively make up an industry, and each differentiates its product and has limited price-setting power. No stated description now defines monopolistic competition.

qs.stem: Perfect competition prevails when the demand of the output of each product is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A perfectly competitive firm is a price taker in a large market. It can sell additional units at the prevailing market price without lowering that price, so its individual demand curve is horizontal. A horizontal curve has infinite price elasticity.

qs.stem: In monopolistic competition, when firm getting normal profit, what condition should be fulfilled under long period?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: In long-run equilibrium under monopolistic competition, entry removes supernormal profit. Normal profit means total revenue equals total cost, including normal return. Dividing by output gives price equal to average total cost at the chosen output.

qs.stem: If there are many sellers and buyers, goods are not homogeneous, and neither side has complete market knowledge, then there will be

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: “not large” conflicts with the keyed market form; the stem now says there are many buyers and sellers. Many firms sell differentiated products, and participants have imperfect information. Those are standard features of monopolistic competition, unlike perfect competition or monopoly.

qs.stem: Under discriminating monopoly, monopolist will keep his price low, where degree of elasticity of demand is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A discriminating monopolist equates marginal revenue across markets. In a market with more elastic demand, a price rise loses more buyers, so the profitable markup over marginal cost is smaller. The monopolist therefore charges less in that market.

qs.stem: Price discrimination is possible

opts.A: due to the nature of goods
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Price discrimination requires a seller to separate buyers or markets and prevent easy resale. Differences in the service or goods, identifiable customer groups, and legal permission can all enable separate prices. Several listed circumstances can therefore support the practice.

qs.stem: In a perfectly competitive market, there is always

opts.A: Average Revenue (AR) is greater than Marginal Revenue (MR)
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: A competitive firm is a price taker, so each additional unit sells at the market price P. Total revenue is P×Q; average revenue is P and marginal revenue is the change P in total revenue per unit. Hence the two revenues are equal.

qs.stem: In an ordinary single-price monopoly facing a downward-sloping demand curve, there is

opts.A: Average Revenue (AR) is greater than Marginal Revenue (MR)
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: “always” lacked a pricing and demand assumption; the stem now specifies a single-price monopoly with downward-sloping demand. Selling one more unit requires a lower price on all units, so marginal revenue is below the price received per unit. Average revenue equals price; hence AR exceeds MR.

qs.stem: The law of variable proportion is related to

opts.B: Neither short run nor long run
opts.D: Short run

qs.sol: The law varies one input while others remain fixed, a short-run production setting.

qs.stem: On the 'Ridge Lines' marginal productivity of capital and labour are

opts.D: None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

Marginal product measures the change in output caused by a small increase in one input while the other input is held constant.

An isoquant joins input combinations producing equal output. Ridge lines bound the region where both inputs have positive marginal products.

Application

Move along an isoquant toward the limit of useful substitution of an input: the extra output from that input diminishes.

At the boundary for labour, its marginal product reaches zero; at the boundary for capital, capital’s marginal product reaches zero. The respective boundary points across isoquants form the two ridge lines.

Thus the boundary value sought in the question is zero. …

“Only (A) is correct” is correct. Average product rises while marginal product exceeds it, so statement (A) holds. Marginal product typically begins declining before average product, so statement (B) reverses the order. “Both (A) and (B) are correct” fails because the second statement is false because marginal product turns first.

“SMC = TC/quantity” is correct. Marginal cost is the change in total cost per change in output, not TC/quantity. The latter is average total cost, while SAC = AVC+AFC is valid. “SAC = AVC+AFC” fails because average total cost is the sum of variable and fixed average costs.

qs.stem: Which of the following cost curves is/are rectangular hyperbola in shape?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Average fixed cost curve” is the official answer because With fixed cost constant, AFC = TFC/Q traces a rectangular hyperbola. “Average cost curve” fails because average total cost includes variable cost and is not generally a rectangular hyperbola.

qs.stem: Which of the following is/are NOT a property/ properties of an isoquant curve?

opts.B: Higher isoquant means higher level of production
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Isoquant is concave to origin” is the official answer because Standard isoquants are convex to the origin, not concave. “They never intersect each other” fails because non-intersection is a standard property of isoquants.

qs.stem: Which of the following industries is considered natural mono- polies?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A natural monopoly exists when one firm can supply the entire market more efficiently because of very large fixed costs and economies of scale.

Railways and electricity production require extensive infrastructure and have high fixed costs, making them natural monopolies. Banking does not fit this category. Therefore, more than one of the above is applicable.

qs.stem: What is constant along an isoquant? (I) Level of labour (II) Level of capital

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

“None of the above” is correct: Output, rather than either named input, stays constant on one isoquant. “Only I” is wrong here: labour changes as one moves along an isoquant. “Depends on situation of isoquant” is wrong here: location does not make either input individually fixed.

qs.stem: In the law of variable proportions, where is the point of change of trend?

opts.A: Where total product starts increasing at a decreasing rate
opts.B: Where total product starts decreasing at a decreasing rate
opts.C: Where total product starts increasing at an increasing rate
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Where total product starts increasing at a decreasing rate” marks the inflection where total product still rises but at a declining rate. “Where total product starts decreasing at a decreasing rate” describes decline of total product, a later stage.

qs.stem: Rent for warehouses is a component of what cost?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “Distribution cost” includes warehousing and the movement of finished goods. “Production cost” is associated with making the good before warehousing.

उत्पादक-संतुलन का नियम है कि सम-लागत रेखा आइसोक्वेंट को स्पर्श करे।

इस बिंदु पर दिए गए लागत में अधिकतम उत्पादन या दिए गए उत्पादन की न्यूनतम लागत प्राप्त होती है। इसलिए उत्तर है: आइसोक्वेंट के स्पर्शरेखा है।
लघु अवधि में कुछ उत्पादन-साधन स्थिर रहते हैं और कम-से-कम एक साधन परिवर्तनीय होता है। इसलिए लघु अवधि उत्पादन फलन परिवर्तनशील अनुपात के नियम पर आधारित होता है। अतः उत्तर: परिवर्तनशील अनुपात का नियम।

अवधारणा

कुल उत्पाद तब अधिकतम होता है जब सीमांत उत्पाद शून्य हो जाता है।

अनुप्रयोग

परिवर्तनीय अनुपात के नियम में सीमांत उत्पाद के शून्य होने पर कुल उत्पाद अपनी अधिकतम अवस्था में पहुँचता है। अतः उत्तर है: **शून्य**।

qs.stem: When marginal production increases then total production

opts.D: None of these

qs.sol: Marginal production is the additional output from each extra unit of input. If it increases, each successive unit adds more output than the previous one, so total production rises at an increasing rate. Therefore, the answer is “Increases by increasing rate.”

qs.stem: Continuous substitutability of capital and labour is shown by

opts.D: Concave isoquant curve

qs.sol: Continuous substitutability means capital can replace labour, and vice versa, in varying proportions. This is represented by a smooth, convex isoquant curve.

qs.stem: The law of variable proportions comes into being when

opts.A: There are only two variable factors
opts.B: There is a fixed factor and a variable factor
opts.D: Variable factors yield less

qs.sol: The law of variable proportions applies when one factor remains fixed while another factor is varied. Here, production changes as the variable factor is combined with a fixed factor. Hence, it comes into being when there is a fixed factor and a variable factor.

qs.stem: The law of variable proportions assumes

opts.A: When marginal cost falls, total production will decrease
opts.B: Utility is maximised when marginal production falls
opts.C: Some factors of production are fixed
opts.D: When marginal production falls, total production is maximum

qs.sol: The law of variable proportions applies when some factors remain fixed while at least one factor varies. Therefore, the applicable statement is: Some factors of production are fixed.

qs.stem: If total production increases with the increase in variable factor, it is called

opts.D: Law of supply of production

qs.sol: The law of increasing returns applies when total production rises as the variable factor increases. Here, total production increases with an increase in the variable factor; therefore, the answer is Law of increasing return.

दीर्घकालीन औसत कुल लागत पहले पैमाने की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं के कारण घटती है और बाद में पैमाने की विसंगतियों के कारण बढ़ती है। इसी घटने-बढ़ने से इसका वक्र तश्तरी के आकार का बनता है। अतः उत्तर है: पैमाने की अर्थव्यवस्थाएँ और विसंगतियाँ।

qs.stem: Production Function refers to

opts.D: Shifting of tax

qs.sol:
A production function shows the relationship between inputs used in production and the output produced, given the technology.

Inputs such as labour and capital are used to produce goods or services. Hence, the answer is Relationship between input and output.

qs.stem: Long run Average Total Cost curve is saucer shaped due to

opts.C: Law of variable proportions and    Economies and diseconomies of scale both
opts.D: None of these

qs.sol:
The long-run average total cost curve is shaped by economies and diseconomies of scale, since all inputs can vary in the long run.

Economies of scale lower average cost as output expands.

Average cost remains nearly constant over a range of output, forming the flat base of the saucer.

Diseconomies of scale eventually raise average cost.

Thus, the answer is Economies and diseconomies of scale. The law of variable proportions applies to the short run, when some inputs are fixed.

qs.stem: Production function is the relation of

opts.D: Price and Demand

qs.sol:
A production function describes the relationship between inputs used in production and the output produced.

Inputs such as labour and capital are combined to produce goods or services. Hence, the answer is Input and Output.

qs.stem: When average cost falls, as a result of increase in output the marginal cost is

opts.D: None of the above

qs.sol:
Marginal cost pulls average cost down when it is below average cost.

Here, average cost falls as output increases. Therefore, marginal cost is less than average cost.

opts.D: MC curve

qs.sol:
Average fixed cost falls continuously as output increases because the same fixed cost is spread over more units.

topics.deep:
- **Production function:** Q = f(L, K, ...). Short run: at least one factor fixed; long run: all variable. **Law of variable proportions:** with one variable factor added to fixed factors:
| Stage | MP | TP |
|---|---|---|
| I - Increasing returns | Rising up to max | Increases at increasing rate |
| II - Diminishing returns | Falling but positive | Increases at decreasing rate, reaches maximum when MP = 0 |
| III - Negative returns | Negative | Falls |
The rational producer operates in Stage II. **AP and MP:** when MP > AP, AP rises; MP cuts AP at AP's maximum. If MP is positive, TP rises.
- **Assumptions:** one factor variable, homogeneous units, technology constant. **Returns to scale** (long run): increasing, constant, decreasing; economies of scale: internal and external.
- **Isoquants:** curve of input combinations giving equal output; slopes down, convex to origin, does not intersect, higher isoquant = more output. **MRTS(L for K) = -DK/DL = MPL/MPK**; diminishing along the isoquant. Perfect substitutes -> straight-line isoquant; fixed proportions -> L-shaped. **Ridge lines** are loci of points where MP of a factor is zero; the economic region lies between them. Isocost line: all input combinations with same total cost. **Producer equilibrium** (least-cost combination): isocost tangent to isoquant, MPL/w = MPK/r, MRTS = w/r. **Technical efficiency** = maximum output from given physical inputs; economic efficiency = producing at minimum cost.
- **Cost concepts:** Fixed (rent of warehouse) and variable costs; explicit/implicit; opportunity cost. TC = TFC + TVC; AC = TC/Q; AVC = TVC/Q; AFC = TFC/Q (rectangular hyperbola); MC = DTC/DQ.
- **Shape and relationships:** SAC, AVC and SMC are U-shaped (due to law of variable proportions); MC cuts AVC and AC at their minimum points; when AC falls, MC is below AC; when AC rises MC is above. Example: output 10, TC 100 (AC 10); output 11, TC 112: MC = 12 > AC, so AC rises to 10.18.
- **Long-run cost:** LAC is U-shaped (envelope of SACs; planning curve) because of economies of scale first, then diseconomies.
- **Market forms:**
| Feature | Perfect competition | Monopoly | Monopolistic competition | Oligopoly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sellers | Very many | One | Many | Few |
| Product | Homogeneous | No close substitute | Differentiated | Homogeneous or differentiated |
| Entry | Free | Blocked | Free | Restricted |
| Demand curve | Horizontal (firm) | Downward | Downward, elastic | Kinked (Sweezy) |
| Price | Taker; P = MR = AR | Maker; AR > MR | Some control | Interdependence |
- **Equilibrium:** MC = MR with MC cutting MR from below. Perfect competition: LR normal profit, P = min AC. Monopoly: supernormal profits possible. Monopolistic competition (Chamberlin/Robinson): normal profit in long run at tangency of AR and AC, with excess capacity; selling costs (advertising) important. Example (monopoly): P = 20 - Q, MR = 20 - 2Q, MC = 4 -> Q = 8, P = 12.
- **Price discrimination:** charging different prices for same product (first, second, third degree). Conditions: separate markets, different elasticities, no resale; monopolist charges **lower price where elasticity of demand is higher** and higher price where elasticity is lower; equilibrium MC = MR1 = MR2 (combined MR).
- **Monopoly features:** single seller, price maker, entry barriers; **natural monopoly** (railways, electricity distribution) due to large fixed costs and falling LAC. Ordinary single-price monopoly faces downward sloping demand; MR below price.
- **Pricing methods:** cost-plus (mark-up), going-rate, penetration and skimming.
- **Perfect competition equilibrium note:** in perfectly competitive market there is always a uniform price and firms are price takers; demand for each firm's output is perfectly elastic (Mrs Joan Robinson's definition).

**Likely question angles:** (1) Stages of variable proportions. (2) Relation between AP and MP. (3) Properties of isoquants (what is NOT a property). (4) Meaning of MRTS/ridge lines. (5) Shape of AFC, SMC, LAC curves. (6) MC-AC relationship numericals. (7) Condition for equilibrium of monopoly or monopolistic competitor. (8) Statement that is NOT true for monopolistic competition. (9) Conditions for price discrimination and where price is low. (10) Features of perfect competition.

topics.title: 10. Business Finance, Banking, Law & Taxation
topics.theory:
- **Sources of finance:** long term (equity, preference, debentures, retained earnings, term loans, **venture capital** for high-risk tech ventures, ADR/GDR), short term (trade credit, bank credit, commercial paper).
- **Equity shareholders** are the primary risk bearers (owners); debenture holders are creditors; **debt gives tax benefit** (interest deductible).
- **Capital structure** = mix of debt and equity; **leverage:** OL = Contribution/EBIT, FL = EBIT/EBT, CL = OL x FL. **MM theory** (no taxes): value of firm independent of capital structure.
- **Working capital:** Gross = total current assets; **Net = CA - CL**; operating cycle; factors: nature of business, credit policy, seasonality.
- **Money market:** short-term (<1 yr) instruments - T-bills, CP, CD, call money; **capital market:** long-term.
- **RBI** est. 1 April 1935; SBI formed 1955; NABARD 1982; IFCI 1948. **Demat** accounts via depositories (NSDL/CDSL); broker issues **contract note**.
- **E-banking:** RTGS (real time gross settlement), NEFT, IMPS, **UPI**.
- **Insurance principles:** utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, contribution (multiple insurance), subrogation.
- **IPR:** patent, trademark, copyright, design, GI. **Consumer Protection Act 2019:** three-tier commissions (District, State, National).
- **Taxation:** ITR = Income Tax Return; Sec 80G donations; GST since 2017; tax holiday = exemption for 5-10 years.
- **Foreign trade:** documents - invoice, bill of lading, bill of entry, letter of credit; EPCG scheme allows import of capital goods at concessional duty.

opts.D:

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A proforma invoice is a preliminary quotation sent before a sale and specifies the offered goods.

qs.stem: When one party grants the other party, the right to use the asset in return for a periodic payment, it is known as

A lease separates the right to use an asset from its ownership: the lessor grants use and the lessee makes periodic payments.

Factoring concerns receivables and trade credit concerns deferred payment for goods, so neither fits this asset-use arrangement.

qs.stem: A dispute where the person against whom a complaint has been made, denies or disputes the allegation contained in the complaint [Section 2(1)(e)] is referred to as

More than one of the above

E

qs.sol: Section 2(1)(e) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 defines a consumer dispute as a dispute where the person complained against denies or disputes the allegations. The wording in the stem follows that statutory definition.

qs.stem: Which of the following serves as an intermediary between the investor and the depository who is authorized to maintain the accounts of dematerialized shares?

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A depository holds securities in electronic form and maintains records through its participants.

qs.stem: Which of the following documents is required in connection with an import transaction?

More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The BPSC final Series A key marks “Letter of Credit” for this printed question. A letter of credit is a bank undertaking to pay the exporter when its documentary conditions are met.

qs.stem: A distinctive sign which identifies certain goods or services as those produced or provided by a specific person or enterprise is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A trademark is a distinctive sign that identifies the commercial origin of goods or services.

Patents protect inventions, while copyright protects original creative expression; neither is the sign described.

qs.stem: Identify the correct sequence of steps to be followed in the trading procedure at stock exchange.

opts.B: Settlement of order, opening a trading account and demat account, placing an order, execution of order

Trading begins by opening trading and demat accounts.

An investor then places an order, which the exchange executes on a match.

Settlement transfers securities and funds after execution.

More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:

qs.stem: An exclusive right granted for an invention, which is a product or a process that provides, in general, a new way of doing something or offers a new technical solution to a problem, is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A patent protects a novel invention, whether a product or a process.

It grants an exclusive right over a technical solution for a limited period.

The description therefore identifies a patent.

qs.stem: ——— was set up with prime objective of professionalizing the country’s foreign trade management by providing training, research and data dissemination.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade was established to strengthen India's foreign-trade management through education, research and information dissemination.

The stated training and research remit identifies the institution rather than an export-sector council or trade-fair promoter.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is false?

opts.C: Trademarks are protected under the Consumer Protection Act.

None of the above

A trademark distinguishes one undertaking’s goods or services and is an intellectual-property right.

The Consumer Protection Act is not the statute that confers trademark registration and protection; that claim is false.

The capital structure decision deals with determining the proportion of debt and equity used to finance the firm’s assets. It focuses on how a company raises funds — whether through borrowed funds (debt) or owners’ funds (equity) — to achieve an optimal balance that minimizes the cost of capital and maximizes the value of the firm.

A Revocable Letter of Credit can be amended or canceled by the issuing bank without prior notice or consent of the exporter (beneficiary). It provides less security to the exporter because the terms can be changed at any time before payment is made.

qs.stem: Which of the following sentences explains the principle of utmost good faith in insurance?

opts.A: Premium is computed on the basis of the assessment of the proposal form.
opts.B: A person who enters into contract has a legal obligation to act with honesty.
opts.C: It is mainly concerned with how the losses or damages happen.
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Utmost good faith requires insurance parties to deal honestly and disclose material facts affecting the risk.

The proposer must give truthful information before the insurer accepts and prices the risk; the duty concerns conduct in the contract.

qs.stem: Which of the following documents is not required for obtaining export license?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
An export authorization is obtained before an overseas sale, whereas a letter of credit is a payment undertaking arranged for a particular buyer-seller transaction.

qs.stem: Gross working capital refers to

qs.sol: A business commonly uses a current account for frequent banking transactions and withdrawals. “Account current” is a statement of mutual transactions, not the bank deposit account meant here. A savings account is normally intended for personal saving.

qs.stem:
Consider the following statements about the international financial sources:

I. A Global Depository Receipt (GDR) is a bank certificate issued in more than one country for shares in a foreign country.

II. A GDR is very similar to American Depository Receipt (ADR).

Select the correct option.

opts.A: Statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect
opts.B: Statement II is correct and statement I is incorrect
opts.C: Both statements I and II are correct
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A GDR is a depositary bank certificate representing shares of a foreign company and may be offered across markets.

An ADR is the related US-market depositary receipt; both represent underlying foreign shares through a depositary arrangement.

They are similar instruments even though their market scope differs.

qs.stem: When a property is insured by more than one insurance (i.e., in case of multiple insurance), the insurers are to share losses in what proportion?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: The principle of contribution applies when the same property and risk are covered by several insurers. Each insurer contributes to an indemnified loss in the ratio of its sum insured to the total sums insured. Premium amounts need not track those coverage limits.

qs.stem: Which among the following is an allied service provided by a bank?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

None of the above

qs.sol: Banks provide auxiliary services in addition to accepting deposits and lending. Safe-deposit lockers protect customers’ valuables, while underwriting supports securities issues. qs.stem: ——— help to integrate formal credit systems into rural societies to encourage the habit of savings among the poor.

None of the above

Members of a self-help group make regular small savings and pool them, then link the group with a bank for formal credit.

This collective saving and bank-linkage model brings low-income rural households into formal finance.

qs.stem: The Government of India proposed to encourage the e-transactions by encouraging the use of plastic money (through debit, credit and gift cards) or net banking by allowing deductions in usage charges, fees and income-tax exemptions. Usage charges, fees and tax exemptions are financial policy tools that affect business transactions.

The relevant business-environment component is therefore economic.

It is calculated as current assets minus current liabilities.

qs.stem: What is the purpose of crowd funding as a method of raising funds?

It gives a project or venture access to a broad crowd of funders rather than relying on a single institution.

None of the above

Government bond markets enable issuance and secondary trading of sovereign debt securities. Company shares are equity, while private issuers’ bonds belong to a different issuer category.

qs.stem: What is the role of stock exchange in financial markets?

opts.C: Offering investment advisory services to the investors
opts.D:

qs.stem: _____ refers to the structure of total capital funds raised by the company.

More than one of the above

None of the above

qs.stem: Which of the following is relevant while planning for working capital requirement?

opts.B: A scheme that provides financial assistance to exporters for marketing their products in foreign countries

opts.D:

qs.stem: Which source of finance provides benefit in tax ?

Note on the answer key: KVS published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Debentures”. This question is graded by the provisional key, as in the actual exam.

“Debentures” can provide a tax benefit because interest paid on them is ordinarily a deductible business expense. “Preference Shares” pay dividends from profit rather than deductible interest.

qs.stem: Trade credit is provided by

Note on the answer key: KVS published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Supplier”. This question is graded by the provisional key, as in the actual exam.

“Supplier” grants trade credit by supplying goods or services with payment due later. “Commercial Bank” extends bank credit, which is different from the supplier’s payment terms.

qs.stem: Excess of 'Current Assets' over 'Current Liabilities' is known as :

opts.D: Gross Working Capital

Note on the answer key: KVS published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Net Working Capital”. This question is graded by the provisional key, as in the actual exam.

qs.stem: Enough working capital is an indicator of which quality of the business ?

Note on the answer key: KVS published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Liquidity”. This question is graded by the provisional key, as in the actual exam.

Liquidity is the ability to meet short-term obligations, for which adequate working capital is an indicator. Growth refers to expansion, and Strength is broader than the short-term payment capacity tested here.

qs.stem: Investment in Equity Shares is?

opts.D:
Non-Profitable

E

None of the above

qs.stem: Which of the following are Short Term Finance?

opts.D:
Bonds

E

None of the above

qs.stem: __________ play a vital role in giving credit access to the poor and this is extremely crucial in poverty alleviation

SHG

None of the above

qs.stem: RBI was established on

opts.D:
5th August 1943

E

None of the above

qs.sol: “1st April 1935” is the date on which the Reserve Bank of India commenced operations. “1st April 1934” is wrong here: The 1934 Act supplied the legal basis, but operations began the following year.

qs.stem: Who is the present Governor of RBI?

Shri K.R. Puri

opts.D:
Anti Depositary Receipts

None of the above

Unified Prepayment Interface

qs.stem: Primary aim of financial management is to _______

opts.B: Maximisation of the market value of equity shares
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT: The primary objective of financial management is to make decisions that increase the owners’ economic value. In a company, this objective is expressed through the market value of the equity shares, because that value reflects expected cash flows, risk, and timing.

APPLICATION: The first three statements describe the same objective at different levels: maximising shareholder wealth, maximising the market value of equity shares, and the wealth-maximisation concept. Each therefore belongs to the objective being tested.

Maximise shareholder’s wealth: states the objective in stakeholder terms. …

qs.stem: The inability of a business to meet its fixed financial obligations,like payment of interest,is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT

Financial risk is the possibility that a firm cannot meet fixed financing obligations, such as interest or principal payments, from its available earnings and cash flow.

APPLICATION

The stem identifies a fixed financial obligation: payment of interest.

It states that the business is unable to meet that obligation.

Inability to service fixed financing charges is the defining situation described by financial risk.

CROSS-CHECK

Business risk concerns uncertainty in operating revenue and costs before financing charges.

Market risk concerns changes in market prices, rates, or demand.

Result: the described situation is financial risk.

qs.stem: When the stock market index is rising,a company may issue in order to meet its financial requirements.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept: In a rising market, investor optimism and demand for ownership financing increase.

Application: A company can issue equity shares to raise capital from investors who accept ownership participation.

Cross-check: Bonds and debentures create debt obligations with fixed repayment or interest, while equity represents ownership. Therefore the relevant security is equity shares.

qs.stem: It is essentially the preparation of a financial blueprint of an organisation's future operations.Identify the related concept.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

Financial planning is the process of estimating an organisation's future financial needs and preparing a coordinated financial blueprint for its operations.

Application

The stem describes preparation of a financial blueprint for future operations. That definition identifies financial planning, which sets expected funds, uses and timing before operations are carried out.

Contrast

Capital budgeting decisions concern choosing and evaluating long-term investments and assets.

Financial management is the broader function of obtaining, allocating and controlling funds. …

qs.stem: Which of the following is not an objective of financial planning?

opts.B: Ensuring enough funds are available at the right time
opts.C: Ensuring excess availability of funds at the right time.
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT

Financial planning sets financial objectives and determines the funds needed to achieve them.

APPLICATION

The objective is to make sufficient funds available when required while avoiding both shortage and idle excess. Ensuring smooth operations and timely availability support this purpose; ensuring excess availability does not, because surplus funds may remain idle and reduce efficiency.

CROSS-CHECK

Financial planning balances adequacy and efficient use of funds, so the excess-funds statement is the exception.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is not true?

opts.A: The cost of debt is higher than cost of equity.
opts.B: The interest paid on debt is not treated as a tax-deductible expense
opts.C: The lender's risk is lower than equity shareholder's risk
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT

In capital structure, debt normally has a lower pre-tax required return because lenders hold senior contractual claims, interest is generally tax-deductible for corporations, and equity receives the residual return and risk.

APPLICATION

The value "The cost of debt is higher than cost of equity" conflicts with the usual seniority and required-return relationship between debt and equity.

The value "The interest paid on debt is not treated as a tax-deductible expense" conflicts with the usual corporate interest tax shield.

The value "The lender's risk is lower than equity shareholder's risk" follows from senior contractual payments and the residual position of equity. …

qs.stem: Name the decision which effects both the profitability and the financial risk.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT: Capital structure is the mix of debt and equity used to finance a firm. Debt creates fixed financial charges, so this mix affects owners’ profitability and financial risk.

APPLICATION: Choosing the debt-equity mix changes interest obligations and the number of shares over which earnings are spread. These changes influence return to equity holders and exposure to financial risk.

CROSS-CHECK / CONTRAST: Capital budgeting selects investments; financial planning coordinates funding needs; the phrase more than one names no distinct financing mechanism. Therefore, the decision affecting both profitability and financial risk is Capital structure decision.

qs.stem: Under which of the following situations a company should not issue debt capital?

opts.A: When the cash flow condition of the company is strong
opts.B: When the rate of tax is low
opts.C: When the return on investment is high
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

Debt financing is attractive when the interest tax shield and the firm’s ability to service debt justify its cost. The tax shield equals the interest deduction multiplied by the applicable tax rate.

Application

Here, a low tax rate makes the interest deduction worth less, so the tax shield from issuing debt is reduced. That weakens one of the main financial reasons to choose debt capital.

Cross-check

Strong cash flow improves repayment capacity.

A high return on investment concerns project profitability.

The combined and none-of-the-above choices do not identify a financing condition by themselves.

Result: the relevant situation is a low tax rate.

qs.stem: The working capital requirement of a business is not likely to be low when

opts.A: The scale of the business operation is small.
opts.B: When the growth prospects of the business are high
opts.C: When the raw material is easily available
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

Working capital is the funds invested in current assets for day-to-day operations. The requirement generally rises with operating scale, growth, and the time needed to obtain inputs and convert them into sales.

Application

A small operating scale limits the inventory, receivables, and cash balances that must be financed.

Easily available raw material shortens the procurement and holding cycle, reducing funds tied up in stock.

High growth prospects require current assets to expand ahead of sales, increasing the operating funds needed. …

qs.stem: Which one of the following could not be registered as a trade mark?

opts.B: The mark is made up of letters and numbers
opts.C: The mark represents the natural or technical shape of the goods.
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: CONCEPT: Trademark registration protects a sign that distinguishes one undertaking’s goods or services. A sign that is merely the natural or technical shape needed for the goods lacks that distinguishing function. APPLICATION: An image can function as a visual sign; letters and numbers can identify commercial origin; and a shape may be registrable when it acts as a badge of origin. A shape representing the natural or technical form of goods is dictated by the product or its technical function, so it cannot serve as a distinctive trademark. CROSS-CHECK/CONTRAST: The image and alphanumeric mark can distinguish source. …

qs.stem: For the PIO to disclose certain information,the Competent  Authority should be satisfied that larger public interest warrants its disclosure. This information pertains to information _____

opts.C: Available to a person in  his fiduciary relationship
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
CONCEPT: The RTI Act permits disclosure of exempt information when larger public interest outweighs the protected interest. Commercial confidence, trade secrets, and fiduciary information are protected categories that may be disclosed under this override.
APPLICATION: Commercial confidence and trade secrets concern protected business information, while fiduciary information is received in a relationship of trust. The competent authority may allow disclosure when larger public interest warrants it.
CROSS-CHECK: All three listed categories are covered by the public-interest override.
RESULT: More than one of the above.

qs.stem: Exemption from paying taxes for 5 years to 10 years is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

A tax holiday is an exemption from paying taxes for a specified period, such as 5 to 10 years.

Tax deduction reduces taxable income, TDS means tax deducted at source, and VAT is value-added tax. None describes a tax holiday.

Therefore, the answer is None of the above.

qs.stem: Which of the following includes owned fund (source of finance for a joint-stock company)?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Owned funds are funds contributed by shareholders or retained from the company’s profits, rather than borrowed funds.

Equity share capital and preference share capital are shareholders’ contributions, so both are owned funds.

Retained earnings are profits kept in the business, so they are also owned funds.

Thus, the answer is More than one of the above.

qs.stem: Companies generally invite public deposits for a period up to

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E

Companies generally accept public deposits for a period of up to 3 years.

Neither 5 years, 4 years nor 10 years matches this limit. Hence, the answer is None of the above.

qs.stem: Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) was established in

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
IFCI was established to provide medium- and long-term finance to industrial enterprises in India.

It was established on 1 July 1948. Therefore, the answer is July 1948.

qs.stem: ADRs are issued in

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) are issued by US depositary banks in the United States to represent shares of foreign companies.

Thus, ADRs are issued in the USA.
चालू सम्पत्तियों में से चालू दायित्व घटाने पर कार्यशील पूँजी प्राप्त होती है। इसलिए चालू सम्पत्तियों का चालू दायित्व पर आधिक्य **कार्यशील पूँजी** कहलाता है।

अवधारणा

भारतीय स्टेट बैंक का गठन 1955 में हुआ था।

अनुप्रयोग

प्रश्न में दिए गए वर्षों में 1955 ही सही वर्ष है।

आयकर नियम के अनुसार केवल कानून में निर्दिष्ट आय ही कर-मुक्त होती है। स्थानीय सत्ता, सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त अस्पताल तथा सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त विश्वविद्यालय/शिक्षण संस्थाओं की आय निर्धारित शर्तों पर कर-मुक्त है। इसके विपरीत, प्रैक्टिस नहीं करने के लिए मिलने वाला भत्ता सामान्यतः वेतन का करयोग्य भाग होता है।

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a source of finance for a company ?

opts.D: Debentures

qs.sol: A source of finance is a means through which a company raises funds. Equity share capital, preference share capital, and debentures provide funds to the company. Fixed assets are resources purchased or owned by the company, not a source of finance.

qs.stem: According to Modigliani and Miller (MM) theory under no taxes, the value of a firm is :

opts.D: Directly proportional to operating income

qs.sol: Under MM theory with no taxes, a firm's value depends on its operating income and business risk, not on how it is financed. Therefore, the value is independent of capital structure.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of lease financing over term loans?

opts.C: No impact on the asset side of the balance sheet
opts.D: Avoids upfront capital investment

qs.sol: Lease financing allows a business to use an asset without purchasing it outright at the beginning. Unlike a term loan used to buy an asset, it generally avoids a large upfront capital investment. Therefore, the advantage is: Avoids upfront capital investment.

qs.stem: In EBIT-EPS analysis, the point of indifference is defined as the level of EBIT at which :

opts.B: EPS under the two financing options is the same
opts.D: Capital structure is optimum

qs.sol:
The EBIT–EPS indifference point is the level of EBIT at which two financing alternatives yield equal earnings per share.

Thus, at this point, neither financing option gives a higher EPS. The answer is: EPS under the two financing options is the same.

qs.stem: Which combination indicates combined leverage in a firm?

opts.D: Sales / Contribution

qs.sol:
Combined leverage measures the effect of fixed operating and financial costs together. It is calculated as:

qs.stem: The relationship between liquidity and risk is

opts.D: none of these

qs.sol:
Liquidity is the ease of converting an asset into cash without significant loss. Higher liquidity reduces the risk of being unable to meet payment obligations.

Thus, as liquidity increases, risk decreases: the relationship is inverse.

qs.stem: From following which is a Public Sector Bank?

opts.D: AXIS

qs.sol:
A public sector bank is a bank in which the government holds a majority stake.

SBI (State Bank of India) is majority-owned by the Government of India. ICICI and Axis Bank, formerly UTI Bank, are private sector banks.

Therefore, the answer is SBI.

qs.stem: Gross Working Capital represents -

opts.D: Excess of Current Assets over Current Liabilities

qs.sol:
Gross working capital means the total current assets of a business, such as cash, inventory and receivables.

Current liabilities are not deducted; doing so gives net working capital.

Therefore, the answer is Total Current Assets.

qs.stem: Operating cycle period is equal to -

opts.C: Conversion Period + Debtors Collection Period – Creditors Payment Period
opts.D: Material Storage Period + Conversion Period + Finished Goods Storage Period + Debtors Collection Period – Creditors Payment Period

qs.sol:
The net operating cycle measures the time for which funds remain tied up in operations, after allowing for credit received from suppliers.

Add the material storage, conversion, finished goods storage and debtors collection periods. Then subtract the creditors payment period.

Thus, the answer is Material Storage Period + Conversion Period + Finished Goods Storage Period + Debtors Collection Period − Creditors Payment Period.

topics.deep:
- **Financial management:** objective is wealth maximisation; three decisions - investment, financing, dividend. Financial planning = blueprint of future financial operations; inadequate planning leads to financial distress, and insolvency = inability to meet fixed obligations (interest, instalments).
- **Sources of finance:**
| Period | Sources |
|---|---|
| Long-term | Equity, preference shares, debentures, retained earnings, term loans, venture capital, lease, ADR/GDR, FCCB |
| Medium | Public deposits (up to 3 years), loans |
| Short-term | Trade credit, bank overdraft, cash credit, commercial paper, factoring |
Equity holders are the primary risk bearers (owners' funds); **venture capital** funds high-risk, high-technology ventures; debt offers tax advantage (interest deductible), lease avoids large initial outlay; **crowd funding** raises small sums from many.
- **Capital structure:** total of equity + debt. Leverage:
| Type | Formula |
|---|---|
| Operating | Contribution/EBIT |
| Financial | EBIT/EBT (EBIT/(EBIT - Interest)) |
| Combined | OL x FL = Contribution/EBT |
**Trading on equity:** using debt to raise EPS if ROI > interest rate. **EBIT-EPS analysis:** indifference point = EBIT at which EPS equal under two financing plans. **MM theory** (no taxes): firm's value independent of capital structure. Debt is cheaper than equity (lender risk lower), so cost of debt < cost of equity. Debt should be avoided when earnings are unstable.
- **Working capital:** Gross = total current assets; Net = CA - CL. Operating cycle = raw material + WIP + finished goods + debtors periods - creditors period. Requirement is higher with long production cycle, liberal credit and seasonal business; lower with fast turnover, cash sales. Example: CA 5,00,000, CL 3,00,000 -> NWC 2,00,000.
- **Financial markets:** money market (up to 1 year; T-bills, CP, CD, call money; liquidity vs risk - more liquid, less risky); capital market (primary and secondary). **SEBI** regulates; stock exchange provides liquidity and price discovery. Trading: broker -> order -> contract note (within 24 hours) -> settlement (T+1) -> demat account through depository participant (NSDL, CDSL). Government bond market finances government deficit.
- **Banking:** RBI (est. 1 April 1935; nationalised 1949) is central bank; commercial banks - savings, current, fixed, recurring deposits; sweep-in account moves surplus above a limit into FD. Allied services: lockers, ATMs, safe custody, payments. Microfinance and SHGs integrate poor with credit. Development institutions: IFCI (1948), SIDBI, NABARD (1982). SBI formed 1955. E-banking: RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI.
- **Insurance:** principles - utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, subrogation, contribution (multiple insurance: each insurer pays ratably), proximate cause.
- **IPR:** patent (inventions; 20 years), trademark (sign identifying goods/services; protected under Trade Marks Act 1999; renewable every 10 years), copyright (literary, artistic works, life + 60 years), design, GI. RTI Act 2005.
- **Consumer Protection Act 2019:** District, State and National Commissions; complainant = consumer, member, association; complaint admissibility decided within 21 days; reliefs include replacement, refund, compensation. Central Consumer Protection Authority.
- **Taxation:** income tax (direct) - ITR, PAN, Sec 80G deductions (100% for national funds like National Sports Fund); GST (July 2017) replaced many indirect taxes; tax holidays exempt units for 5 to 10 years; customs duty on imports.
- **Foreign trade:** import documents - invoice, bill of lading, bill of entry, import licence, letter of credit; export - shipping bill, certificate of origin. Revocable LC may be changed by issuing bank without notice. EPCG: concessional/zero duty capital goods against export obligation. DGFT regulates foreign trade; IIFT trains.

**Likely question angles:** (1) Net working capital/gross working capital definitions. (2) Source with tax benefit; primary risk bearer. (3) Venture capital, crowd funding purpose. (4) Leverage formula combination. (5) Indifference point in EBIT-EPS. (6) Depository participant and contract note. (7) Full forms: RTGS, ADR, GDR, UPI, CIN. (8) Insurance principle identification. (9) IPR type for a given item. (10) Consumer commission procedure and import/export documents.

topics.title: 11. Business Mathematics & Statistics
topics.theory:
- **Mean, median, mode:** Mean = Sum/n; median = middle value of sorted data; mode = most frequent; **Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean** (empirical).
- **Dispersion:** Range, Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2, Mean deviation, **Standard deviation**, Variance, CV = SD/Mean x 100. In a normal distribution QD = 2/3 SD.
- **Data:** primary (first-hand, via interview/questionnaire/observation) vs secondary; Census conducted by Registrar General, every 10 years.
- **Classification:** chronological (time), geographical, qualitative, quantitative.
- **Sampling:** random, **stratified** (population divided into mutually exclusive groups), cluster, systematic; sampling error decreases as sample size rises.
- **Index numbers:** base year value = **100**; Laspeyres (base-year weights), Paasche (current-year weights), **Fisher = sqrt(L x P)**.
- **Time series:** secular trend, seasonal (within a year), cyclical, irregular. Forecasting: moving average, exponential smoothing, regression.
- **Probability** = favourable/total outcomes; leap year has 52 weeks + 2 odd days.
- **Compound interest:** A = P(1 + r)^n.
- **Matrices/Calculus:** A(adj A) = |A| I; d/dx(cos^-1 x) = -1/sqrt(1 - x^2); quadratic y = ax^2 + bx + c (a != 0).
- **Proportion:** componendo, dividendo, alternendo, invertendo, subtrahendo.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of applying statistical forecasting methods?

opts.A: These are always better than experts’ “best guesses.”
opts.B: These are particularly useful in providing prior information about important events that have no historical precedent.
opts.C: These are more accurate than purely judgmental techniques when sufficient data is available.
opts.D: These are particularly useful in dynamic environments.

qs.sol: Concept: Forecasting techniques fall into two broad families — judgmental (qualitative) methods, which rely on expert opinion and contextual knowledge, and statistical (quantitative) methods, which apply mathematical models such as time-series analysis and regression to historical data. Statistical methods are the better choice once sufficient, stable historical data exists; judgmental methods are preferred when data is sparse, the event is unprecedented, or conditions are changing quickly. …

qs.stem: The time period for which an index number is determined, is known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
An index number compares a target period with a reference period.

The target period whose level is being measured is the current period; the reference is the base period.

qs.stem: Data represented through arithmetic line graph helps in understanding

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
An arithmetic line graph plots a variable's values in chronological order and joins the points.

The overall direction across a long span exposes the underlying long-term trend; cycles and seasonal effects require repeated-pattern analysis.

qs.stem: Which general category of data consists of first-hand observations collected for the investigator's present study?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Modified from the original question: ‘data set of first-hand information’ could also describe data produced by a census; the stem now asks for the general category rather than a collection method.

Data gathered directly for a present purpose are primary data. A census can produce such data, but names complete enumeration, not a general source category.

qs.stem: An investor deposits ₹ 600 in a bank and plans to leave it there for four years. The value of the account after four years if it earns 10% simple interest per year for this period will be

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Simple interest equals principal × annual rate × time = ₹600 × 0.10 × 4 = ₹240. Add this to the unchanged principal: maturity value = ₹600 + ₹240 = ₹840.

qs.stem: In a chronological classification, the data are classified on the basis of

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Chronological means arranged in temporal order, such as figures by year or month. A chronological classification therefore groups observations by their date or period. Attributes and class intervals are different classification bases.

qs.stem: Data originally collected for an investigation are known as

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Data collected first-hand for the specific investigation are primary data. Data taken from an existing publication are secondary; pooled data combine observations across units and time. The phrase “originally collected” identifies the first-hand category.

qs.stem: “Statistics is a science of estimates and probabilities.” This definition is given by

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Boddington described statistics through estimation of unknown quantities and probability of uncertain events. The quoted wording is attributed to him, rather than the broader dictionary or economic definitions of the other authors.

1

qs.sol: “100” is the conventional index-number value assigned to the base year. “1” is wrong here: One is possible for a ratio but not the convention used for the stated index.

qs.stem: According to the important properties Subtrahendo of proportion

opts.A: If a : b = c : d, then a + c : b + d
opts.B: If a : b = c : d, then a – c : b – d
opts.C: If a : b = c : d, then a – b : b = c – d : d
opts.D:
If a : b = c : d, then a + b : b = c + d : d

E

If a : b = c : d, then a : c = b : d

qs.sol: “If a : b = c : d, then a – c : b – d” subtracts corresponding antecedents and consequents of an equal proportion. “If a : b = c : d, then a – b : b = c – d : d” is wrong here: This subtracts each antecedent from its consequent and describes a different property.

opts.D: Free Hand Curve Method

qs.sol: Secular trend is measured using methods such as moving averages, semi-averages, and freehand curves. The weighted average method is not a standard method for measuring secular trend; therefore, the answer is Weighted Average Method.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a technique of Business Forecasting ?

opts.D: Profit planning

qs.sol: Business forecasting techniques help estimate and plan future business performance. Budgeting, determination of cost standards, and profit planning support this process. Presentation of financial statements mainly reports financial information, so it is not a forecasting technique.

opts.B: Under time series forecast data obtained from past experience is analyzed
